It is highly recommended to not set this value below 10, as it generates a very large number of boring locations and items.
In the worst case, it is 1500+ checks for a single coin

options.name: time_is_money
options.description:
Whether the Time is Money pack is considered required to complete the grindstone.
If optional, you may be expected to grind 10 000 times by hand

options.name: double_jump_glitch
options.description: Whether to include the double jump glitches in logic. Separated between the simple ones and the very difficult ones

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Choose the main goal.
complete_all_levels: All levels of the selected episodes
complete_boss_levels: Boss levels (E#M8) of selected episodes

options.name: difficulty
options.description:
Choose the game difficulty. These options match DOOM's skill levels.
baby (I'm too young to die.) Same as easy, with double ammo pickups and half damage taken.
easy (Hey, not too rough.) Less monsters or strength.
medium (Hurt me plenty.) Default.
hard (Ultra-Violence.) More monsters or strength.
nightmare (Nightmare!) Monsters attack more rapidly and respawn.

options.name: random_monsters
options.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Monsters are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small monsters vs medium vs big)
random_chaotic: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the entire game.

options.name: random_pickups
options.description:
Choose how pickups are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Pickups are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Pickups are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small pickups vs Big)

options.name: random_music
options.description:
Level musics will be randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle_selected: Selected episodes' levels will be shuffled
shuffle_game: All the music will be shuffled

options.name: flip_levels
options.description:
Flip levels on one axis.
vanilla: No flipping
flipped: All levels are flipped
randomly_flipped: Random levels are flipped

options.name: allow_death_logic
options.description:
Some locations require a timed puzzle that can only be tried once.
After which, if the player failed to get it, the location cannot be checked anymore.
By default, no progression items are placed here. There is a way, hovewer, to still get them:
Get killed in the current map. The map will reset, you can now attempt the puzzle again.

options.name: pro
options.description:
Include difficult tricks into rules. Mostly employed by speed runners.
i.e.: Leaps across to a locked area, trigger a switch behind a window at the right angle, etc.

options.name: start_with_computer_area_maps
options.description: Give the player all Computer Area Map items from the start.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: reset_level_on_death
options.description:
When dying, levels are reset and monsters respawned. But inventory and checks are kept.
Turning this setting off is considered easy mode. Good for new players that don't know the levels well.

options.name: episode1
options.description:
Knee-Deep in the Dead.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode2
options.description:
The Shores of Hell.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode3
options.description:
Inferno.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode4
options.description:
Thy Flesh Consumed.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: split_backpack
options.description: Split the Backpack into four individual items, each one increasing ammo capacity for one type of weapon only.

options.name: backpack_count
options.description:
How many Backpacks will be available.
If Split Backpack is set, this will be the number of each capacity upgrade available.

options.name: max_ammo_bullets
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for bullets.

options.name: max_ammo_shells
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for shotgun shells.

options.name: max_ammo_rockets
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for rockets.

options.name: max_ammo_energy_cells
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for energy cells.

options.name: added_ammo_bullets
options.description: Set the amount of bullet capacity added when collecting a backpack or capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_shells
options.description: Set the amount of shotgun shell capacity added when collecting a backpack or capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_rockets
options.description: Set the amount of rocket capacity added when collecting a backpack or capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_energy_cells
options.description: Set the amount of energy cell capacity added when collecting a backpack or capacity upgrade.

options.name: max_science_pack
options.description:
Maximum level of science pack required to complete the game.
This also affects the relative cost of silo and satellite recipes if they are randomized.
That is the only thing in which the Utility Science Pack and Space Science Pack settings differ.

options.name: goal
options.description: Goal required to complete the game.

options.name: craftsanity
options.description:
Choose a number of researches to require crafting a specific item rather than with science packs.
May be capped based on the total number of locations.
There will always be at least 2 Science Pack research locations for automation and logistics, and 1 for rocket-silo
if the Rocket Silo option is not set to Spawn.

options.name: silo
options.description: Ingredients to craft rocket silo or auto-place if set to spawn.

options.name: satellite
options.description: Ingredients to craft satellite.

options.name: free_samples
options.description: Get free items with your technologies.

options.name: free_samples_quality
options.description:
If free samples are on, determine the quality of the granted items.
Requires the quality mod, which is part of the Space Age DLC. Without it, normal quality is given.

options.name: starting_items
options.description: Mapping of Factorio internal item-name to amount granted on start.

options.name: free_sample_blacklist
options.description: Set of items that should never be granted from Free Samples

options.name: free_sample_whitelist
options.description: Overrides any free sample blacklist present. This may ruin the balance of the mod, be warned.

options.name: recipe_time
options.description:
Randomize the time it takes for any recipe to craft, this includes smelting, chemical lab, hand crafting etc.
Fast: 0.25X - 1X
Normal: 0.5X - 2X
Slow: 1X - 4X
Chaos: 0.25X - 4X
New category: ignores vanilla recipe time and rolls new one
New Fast: 0.25 - 2 seconds
New Normal: 0.25 - 10 seconds
New Slow:  5 - 10 seconds

options.name: recipe_ingredients
options.description: Select if rocket, or rocket + science pack ingredients should be random.

options.name: recipe_ingredients_offset
options.description:
When randomizing ingredients, remove or add this many "slots" of items.
For example, at -1 a randomized Automation Science Pack will only require 1 ingredient, instead of 2.

options.name: imported_blueprints
options.description: Allow or Disallow Blueprints from outside the current savegame.

options.name: world_gen
options.description:
World Generation settings. Overview of options at https://wiki.factorio.com/Map_generator,
with in-depth documentation at https://lua-api.factorio.com/latest/concepts/MapGenSettings.html

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: energy_link
options.description: Allow sending energy to other worlds. 25% of the energy is lost in the transfer.

options.name: tech_tree_layout
options.description:
Selects how the tech tree nodes are interwoven.
Single: No dependencies
Diamonds: Several grid graphs (4/9/16 nodes each)
Pyramids: Several top halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Funnels: Several bottom halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Trees: Several trees
Choices: A single balanced binary tree

options.name: progressive
options.description:
Merges together Technologies like "automation-1" to "automation-3" into 3 copies of "Progressive Automation",
which awards them in order.

options.name: min_tech_cost
options.description: The cheapest a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.name: max_tech_cost
options.description: The most expensive a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.name: tech_cost_distribution
options.description:
Random distribution of costs of the Science Packs.
Even: any number between min and max is equally likely.
Low: low costs, near the minimum, are more likely.
Middle: medium costs, near the average, are more likely.
High: high costs, near the maximum, are more likely.

options.name: tech_cost_mix
options.description:
Percent chance that a preceding Science Pack is also required.
Chance is rolled per preceding pack.

options.name: ramping_tech_costs
options.description:
Forces the amount of Science Packs required to ramp up with the highest involved Pack. Average is preserved.
For example:
off: Automation (red)/Logistics (green) sciences can range from 1 to 1000 Science Packs,
on: Automation (red) ranges to ~500 packs and Logistics (green) from ~500 to 1000 Science Packs

options.name: tech_tree_information
options.description:
How much information should be displayed in the tech tree.
None: No indication of what a research unlocks.
Advancement: Indicates if a research unlocks an item that is considered logical advancement, but not who it is for.
Full: Labels with exact names and recipients of unlocked items; all researches are prefilled into the !hint command.

options.name: attack_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an attack on your base.

options.name: evolution_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received increase the enemy evolution.

options.name: evolution_trap_increase
options.description:
How much an Evolution Trap increases the enemy evolution.
Increases scale down proportionally to the session's current evolution factor
(40 increase at 0.50 will add 0.20... 40 increase at 0.75 will add 0.10...)

options.name: teleport_traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger a random teleport.
It is ensured the player can walk back to where they got teleported from.

options.name: grenade_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a grenade explosion on each player.

options.name: cluster_grenade_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a cluster grenade explosion on each player.

options.name: artillery_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an artillery shell on each player.

options.name: atomic_rocket_traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on each player.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.name: atomic_cliff_remover_traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on a random cliff.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.name: inventory_spill_traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger dropping your main inventory and trash inventory onto the ground.

options.name: keep_shop_red_potions
options.description:
Prevents the Shop's Red Potions from being shuffled. Those locations
will have purchasable Red Potion as usual for their usual price.

options.name: include_pendant
options.description:
Pendant is an item that boosts your attack power permanently when picked up.
However, due to a programming error in the original game, it has the reverse
effect. You start with the Pendant power, and lose it when picking
it up. So this item is essentially a trap.
There is a setting in the client to reverse the effect back to its original intend.
This could be used in conjunction with this option to increase or lower difficulty.

options.name: include_poisons
options.description:
Whether or not to include Poison Potions in the pool of items. Including them
effectively turn them into traps in multiplayer.

options.name: require_dragon_slayer
options.description:
Requires the Dragon Slayer to be available before fighting the final boss is required.
Turning this on will turn Progressive Shields into progression items.

This setting does not force you to use Dragon Slayer to kill the final boss.
Instead, it ensures that you will have the Dragon Slayer and be able to equip
it before you are expected to beat the final boss.

options.name: random_musics
options.description:
All levels' music is shuffled. Except the title screen because it's finite.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

options.name: random_sounds
options.description:
All sounds are shuffled.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

options.name: random_npcs
options.description:
NPCs and their portraits are shuffled.
This is an aesthetic option and doesn't affect gameplay.

options.name: random_monsters
options.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.
"Vanilla": No randomization
"Level Shuffle": Monsters are shuffled within a level
"Level Random": Monsters are picked randomly, balanced based on the ratio of the current level
"World Shuffle": Monsters are shuffled across the entire world
"World Random": Monsters are picked randomly, balanced based on the ratio of the entire world
"Chaotic": Completely random, except big vs small ratio is kept. Big are mini-bosses.

options.name: random_rewards
options.description: Monsters drops are shuffled.

options.name: locations
options.description: to roll settings go to https://finalfantasyrandomizer.com/

options.name: items
options.description: to roll settings go to https://finalfantasyrandomizer.com/

options.name: rules
options.description: to roll settings go to https://finalfantasyrandomizer.com/

options.name: logic
options.description:
Placement logic sets the rules that will be applied when placing items. Friendly: Required Items to clear a
dungeon will never be placed in that dungeon to avoid the need to revisit it. Also, the Magic Mirror and the Mask
will always be available before Ice Pyramid and Volcano, respectively. Note: If Dungeons are shuffled, Friendly
logic will only ensure the availability of the Mirror and the Mask. Standard: Items are randomly placed and logic
merely verifies that they're all accessible. As for Region access, only the Coins are considered. Expert: Same as
Standard, but Items Placement logic also includes other routes than Coins: the Crests Teleporters, the
Fireburg-Aquaria Lava bridge and the Sealed Temple Exit trick.

options.name: brown_boxes
options.description:
Include the 201 brown box locations from the original game. Brown Boxes are all the boxes that contained a
consumable in the original game. If shuffle is chosen, the consumables contained will be shuffled but the brown
boxes will not be Archipelago location checks.

options.name: sky_coin_mode
options.description:
Configure how the Sky Coin is acquired. With standard, the Sky Coin will be placed randomly. With Start With, the
Sky Coin will be in your inventory at the start of the game. With Save The Crystals, the Sky Coin will be acquired
once you save all 4 crystals. With Shattered Sky Coin, the Sky Coin is split in 40 fragments; you can enter Doom
Castle once the required amount is found. Shattered Sky Coin will force brown box locations to be included.

options.name: shattered_sky_coin_quantity
options.description:
Configure the number of the 40 Sky Coin Fragments required to enter the Doom Castle. Only has an effect if
Sky Coin Mode is set to shattered. Low: 16. Mid: 24. High: 32. Random Narrow: random between 16 and 32.
Random Wide: random between 10 and 38.

options.name: starting_weapon
options.description: Choose your starting weapon.

options.name: progressive_gear
options.description: Pieces of gear are always acquired from weakest to strongest in a set.

options.name: leveling_curve
options.description: Adjust the level gain rate.

options.name: starting_companion
options.description:
Set a companion to start with.
Random Companion: Randomly select one companion.
Random Plus None: Randomly select a companion, with the possibility of none selected.

options.name: available_companions
options.description:
Select randomly which companions will join your party. Unavailable companions can still be reached to get their items and complete their quests if needed.
Note: If a Starting Companion is selected, it will always be available, regardless of this setting.

options.name: companions_locations
options.description:
Set the primary location of companions. Their secondary location is always the same.
Standard: Companions will be at the same locations as in the original game.
Shuffled: Companions' locations are shuffled amongst themselves.
Shuffled Extended: Add all the Temples, as well as Phoebe's House and the Rope Bridge as possible locations.

options.name: kaelis_mom_fight_minotaur
options.description:
Transfer Kaeli's requirements (Tree Wither, Elixir) and the two items she's giving to her mom.
Kaeli will be available to join the party right away without the Tree Wither.

options.name: companion_leveling_type
options.description:
Set how companions gain levels.
Quests: Complete each companion's individual quest for them to promote to their second version.
Quests Extended: Each companion has four exclusive quests, leveling each time a quest is completed.
Save the Crystals (All): Each time a Crystal is saved, all companions gain levels.
Save the Crystals (Individual): Each companion will level to their second version when a specific Crystal is saved.
Benjamin Level: Companions' level tracks Benjamin's.

options.name: companion_spellbook_type
options.description:
Update companions' spellbook.
Standard: Original game spellbooks.
Extended: Add some extra spells. Tristam gains Exit and Quake and Reuben gets Blizzard.
Random Balanced: Randomize the spellbooks with an appropriate mix of spells.
Random Chaos: Randomize the spellbooks in total free-for-all.

options.name: enemies_density
options.description: Set how many of the original enemies are on each map.

options.name: enemies_scaling_lower
options.description: Randomly adjust enemies stats by the selected range percentage. Include mini-bosses' weaker clones.

options.name: enemies_scaling_upper
options.description: Randomly adjust enemies stats by the selected range percentage. Include mini-bosses' weaker clones.

options.name: bosses_scaling_lower
options.description:
Randomly adjust bosses stats by the selected range percentage. Include Mini-Bosses, Bosses, Bosses' refights and
the Dark King.

options.name: bosses_scaling_upper
options.description:
Randomly adjust bosses stats by the selected range percentage. Include Mini-Bosses, Bosses, Bosses' refights and
the Dark King.

options.name: enemizer_attacks
options.description:
Shuffles enemy attacks. Standard: No shuffle. Safe: Randomize every attack but leave out self-destruct and Dark
King attacks. Chaos: Randomize and include self-destruct and Dark King attacks. Self Destruct: Every enemy
self-destructs. Simple Shuffle: Instead of randomizing, shuffle one monster's attacks to another. Dark King is left
vanilla.

options.name: enemizer_groups
options.description: Set which enemy groups will be affected by Enemizer.

options.name: shuffle_res_weak_types
options.description: Resistance and Weakness types are shuffled for all enemies.

options.name: shuffle_enemies_position
options.description: Instead of their original position in a given map, enemies are randomly placed.

options.name: progressive_formations
options.description:
Enemies' formations are selected by regions, with the weakest formations always selected in Foresta and the
strongest in Windia. Disabled: Standard formations are used. Regions Strict: Formations will come exclusively
from the current region, whatever the map is. Regions Keep Type: Formations will keep the original formation type
and match with the nearest power level.

options.name: doom_castle_mode
options.description:
Configure how you reach the Dark King. With Standard, you need to defeat all four bosses and their floors to
reach the Dark King. With Boss Rush, only the bosses are blocking your way in the corridor to the Dark King's room.
With Dark King Only, the way to the Dark King is free of any obstacle.

options.name: doom_castle_shortcut
options.description:
Create a shortcut granting access from the start to Doom Castle at Focus Tower's entrance.
Also modify the Desert floor, so it can be navigated without the Mega Grenades and the Dragon Claw.

options.name: tweak_frustrating_dungeons
options.description:
Make some small changes to a few of the most annoying dungeons. Ice Pyramid: Add 3 shortcuts on the 1st floor.
Giant Tree: Add shortcuts on the 1st and 4th floors and curtail mushrooms population.
Pazuzu's Tower: Staircases are devoid of enemies (regardless of Enemies Density settings).

options.name: map_shuffle
options.description:
None: No shuffle. Overworld: Only shuffle the Overworld locations. Dungeons: Only shuffle the dungeons' floors
amongst themselves. Temples and Towns aren't included. Overworld And Dungeons: Shuffle the Overworld and dungeons
at the same time. Everything: Shuffle the Overworld, dungeons, temples and towns all amongst each others.
When dungeons are shuffled, defeating Pazuzu won't teleport you to the 7th floor, you have to get there normally to
save the Crystal and get Pazuzu's Chest.

options.name: crest_shuffle
options.description: Shuffle the Crest tiles amongst themselves.

options.name: shuffle_battlefield_rewards
options.description:
Shuffle the type of reward (Item, XP, GP) given by battlefields and color code them by reward type.
Blue: Give an item. Grey: Give XP. Green: Give GP.

options.name: map_shuffle_seed
options.description:
If this is a number, it will be used as a set seed number for Map, Crest, Battlefield Reward, and Companion shuffles.
If this is "random" the seed will be chosen randomly. If it is any other text, it will be used as a seed group name.
All players using the same seed group name will get the same shuffle results, as long as their Map Shuffle,
Crest Shuffle, Shuffle Battlefield Rewards, Companion Shuffle, and Kaeli's Mom settings are the same.

options.name: battlefields_battles_quantities
options.description: Adjust the number of battles that need to be fought to get a battlefield's reward.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Choose the main goal.
complete_all_levels: All levels of the selected episodes
complete_boss_levels: Boss levels (E#M8) of selected episodes

options.name: difficulty
options.description:
Choose the game difficulty. These options match Heretic's skill levels.
wet nurse (Thou needeth a wet-nurse) - Fewer monsters and more items than medium. Damage taken is halved, and ammo pickups carry twice as much ammo. Any Quartz Flasks and Mystic Urns are automatically used when the player nears death.
easy (Yellowbellies-r-us) - Fewer monsters and more items than medium.
medium (Bringest them oneth) - Completely balanced, this is the standard difficulty level.
hard (Thou art a smite-meister) - More monsters and fewer items than medium.
black plague (Black plague possesses thee) - Same as hard, but monsters and their projectiles move much faster. Cheating is also disabled.

options.name: random_monsters
options.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Monsters are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small monsters vs medium vs big)
random_chaotic: Monsters are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the entire game.

options.name: random_pickups
options.description:
Choose how pickups are randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle: Pickups are shuffled within the level
random_balanced: Pickups are completely randomized, but balanced based on existing ratio in the level. (Small pickups vs Big)

options.name: random_music
options.description:
Level musics will be randomized.
vanilla: No randomization
shuffle_selected: Selected episodes' levels will be shuffled
shuffle_game: All the music will be shuffled

options.name: allow_death_logic
options.description:
Some locations require a timed puzzle that can only be tried once.
After which, if the player failed to get it, the location cannot be checked anymore.
By default, no progression items are placed here. There is a way, hovewer, to still get them:
Get killed in the current map. The map will reset, you can now attempt the puzzle again.

options.name: pro
options.description:
Include difficult tricks into rules. Mostly employed by speed runners.
i.e.: Leaps across to a locked area, trigger a switch behind a window at the right angle, etc.

options.name: check_sanity
options.description:
Include redundant checks. This increase total check count for the game.
i.e.: In a room, there might be 3 checks close to each other. By default, two of them will be remove.
This was done to lower the total count check for Heretic, as it is quite high compared to other games.
Check Sanity restores original checks.

options.name: start_with_map_scrolls
options.description: Give the player all Map Scroll items from the start.

options.name: reset_level_on_death
options.description:
When dying, levels are reset and monsters respawned. But inventory and checks are kept.
Turning this setting off is considered easy mode. Good for new players that don't know the levels well.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: episode1
options.description:
City of the Damned.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode2
options.description:
Hell's Maw.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode3
options.description:
The Dome of D'Sparil.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode4
options.description:
The Ossuary.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: episode5
options.description:
The Stagnant Demesne.
If none of the episodes are chosen, Episode 1 will be chosen by default.

options.name: split_bag_of_holding
options.description: Split the Bag of Holding into six individual items, each one increasing ammo capacity for one type of weapon only.

options.name: bag_of_holding_count
options.description:
How many Bags of Holding will be available.
If Split Bag of Holding is set, this will be the number of each capacity upgrade available.

options.name: max_ammo_crystals
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for crystals (Elven Wand ammo).

options.name: max_ammo_arrows
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for arrows (Ethereal Crossbow ammo).

options.name: max_ammo_claw_orbs
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for claw orbs (Dragon Claw ammo).

options.name: max_ammo_runes
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for runes (Hellstaff ammo).

options.name: max_ammo_flame_orbs
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for flame orbs (Phoenix Rod ammo).

options.name: max_ammo_spheres
options.description: Set the starting ammo capacity for spheres (Firemace ammo).

options.name: added_ammo_crystals
options.description: Set the amount of crystal capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_arrows
options.description: Set the amount of arrow capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_claw_orbs
options.description: Set the amount of claw orb capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_runes
options.description: Set the amount of rune capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_flame_orbs
options.description: Set the amount of flame orb capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: added_ammo_spheres
options.description: Set the amount of sphere capacity gained when collecting a bag of holding or a capacity upgrade.

options.name: party_shuffle
options.description:
Shuffles party members into the item pool.

Note that enabling this can significantly increase both the difficulty and length of a run.

options.name: gesture_shuffle
options.description: Choose where gestures will appear in the item pool.

options.name: medallion_shuffle
options.description: Shuffles red medallions into the item pool.

options.name: start_location
options.description: Select the starting location from 1 of 4 positions.

options.name: extra_items_in_logic
options.description: Include some extra items in logic (CHARGE UP, 1x PAPER CUP) to prevent the game from becoming too difficult.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

Note that this also includes death by using the PERISH gesture.

Can be toggled via in-game console command "/deathlink".

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: act1_death_link_behaviour
options.description:
If DeathLink is enabled, determines what counts as a death in act 1. This affects deaths sent and received.

- Sacrificed: Send a death when sacrificed by Leshy. Receiving a death will extinguish all candles.

- Candle Extinguished: Send a death when a candle is extinguished. Receiving a death will extinguish a candle.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Defines the goal to accomplish in order to complete the randomizer.

- Full Story In Order: Complete each act in order. You can return to previously completed acts.

- Full Story Any Order: Complete each act in any order. All acts are available from the start.

- First Act: Complete Act 1 by finding the New Game button. Great for a smaller scale randomizer.

options.name: randomize_codes
options.description: Randomize codes and passwords in the game (clocks, safes, etc.)

options.name: randomize_deck
options.description:
Randomize cards in your deck into new cards.
Disable: Disable the feature.

- Every Encounter Within Same Type: Randomize cards within the same type every encounter (keep rarity/scrybe type).

- Every Encounter Any Type: Randomize cards into any possible card every encounter.

- Starting Only: Only randomize cards given at the beginning of runs and acts.

options.name: randomize_sigils
options.description:
Randomize sigils printed on the cards into new sigils every encounter.

- Disable: Disable the feature.

- Randomize Addons: Only randomize sigils added from sacrifices or other means.

- Randomize All: Randomize all sigils.

options.name: optional_death_card
options.description:
Add a moment after death in act 1 where you can decide to create a death card or not.

- Disable: Disable the feature.

- Always On: The choice is always offered after losing all candles.

- DeathLink Only: The choice is only offered after receiving a DeathLink event.

options.name: skip_tutorial
options.description: Skips the first few tutorial runs of act 1. Bones are available from the start.

options.name: skip_epilogue
options.description: Completes the goal as soon as the required acts are completed without the need of completing the epilogue.

options.name: epitaph_pieces_randomization
options.description:
Determines how epitaph pieces in act 2 are randomized. This can affect your chances of getting stuck.

- All Pieces: Randomizes all nine pieces as their own item.

- In Groups: Randomizes pieces in groups of three.

- As One Item: Group all nine pieces as a single item.

options.name: painting_checks_balancing
options.description:
Generation options for the second and third painting checks in act 1.

- None: Adds no progression logic to these painting checks. They will all count as sphere 1 (early game checks).

- Balanced: Adds rules to these painting checks. Early game items are less likely to appear into these paintings.

- Force Filler: For when you dislike doing these last two paintings. Their checks will only contain filler items.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Zero: collect the Heart Stars, and defeat Zero in the Hyper Zone.
Boss Butch: collect the Heart Stars, and then complete the boss rematches in the Boss Butch mode.
MG5: collect the Heart Stars, and then complete a perfect run through the minigame gauntlet within the Super MG5
Jumping: collect the Heart Stars, and then reach a designated score within the Jumping sub-game

options.name: goal_speed
options.description:
Normal: the goal is unlocked after purifying the five bosses
Fast: the goal is unlocked after acquiring the target number of Heart Stars

options.name: max_heart_stars
options.description:
Maximum number of heart stars to include in the pool of items.
If fewer available locations exist in the pool than this number, the number of available locations will be used instead.

options.name: heart_stars_required
options.description:
Percentage of heart stars required to purify the five bosses and reach Zero.
Each boss will require a differing amount of heart stars to purify.

options.name: jumping_target
options.description: The required score needed to complete the Jumping minigame.

options.name: remote_items
options.description: Enables receiving items from your own world, primarily for co-op play.

options.name: strict_bosses
options.description: If enabled, one will not be able to move onto the next world until the previous world's boss has been purified.

options.name: open_world
options.description:
If enabled, all 6 stages will be unlocked upon entering a world for the first time. A certain amount of stages
will need to be completed in order to unlock the bosses

options.name: ow_boss_requirement
options.description: The amount of stages completed needed to unlock the boss of a world when Open World is turned on.

options.name: consumables
options.description: When enabled, adds all 1-Ups and Maxim Tomatoes as possible locations.

options.name: starsanity
options.description:
When enabled, every star in a given stage will become a check.
Will increase the possible filler pool to include 1/3/5 stars.

options.name: filler_percentage
options.description: Percentage of non-required Heart Stars to be converted to filler items (1-Ups, Maxim Tomatoes, Invincibility Candy).

options.name: trap_percentage
options.description: Percentage of filler items to be converted to trap items (Gooey Bags, Slowness, Eject Ability).

options.name: gooey_trap_weight
options.description: Chance that any given trap is a Gooey Bag (spawns Gooey when you receive it).

options.name: slow_trap_weight
options.description: Chance that any given trap is Slowness (halves your max speed for 15 seconds when you receive it).

options.name: ability_trap_weight
options.description: Chance that any given trap is an Eject Ability (ejects your ability when you receive it).

options.name: stage_shuffle
options.description:
None: No stage shuffling.
Same World: shuffles stages around their world.
Pattern: shuffles stages according to the stage pattern (stage 3 will always be a minigame stage, etc.)
Shuffled: shuffles stages across all worlds.

options.name: boss_shuffle
options.description:
None: Bosses will remain in their vanilla locations
Shuffled: Bosses will be shuffled amongst each other
Full: Bosses will be randomized
Singularity: All (non-Zero) bosses will be replaced with a single boss
Supports plando placement.

options.name: animal_randomization
options.description:
Disabled: all animal positions will be vanilla.
Shuffled: all animal positions will be shuffled amongst each other.
Full: random animals will be placed across the levels. At least one of each animal is guaranteed.

options.name: copy_ability_randomization
options.description:
Disabled: enemies give regular copy abilities and health.
Enabled: all enemies will have the copy ability received from them randomized.
Enabled Plus Minus: enemies (except minibosses) can additionally give you anywhere from +2 health to -1 health when eaten.

options.name: boss_requirement_random
options.description:
If enabled, boss purification will require a random amount of Heart Stars. Depending on options, this may have
boss purification unlock in a random order.

options.name: gifting
options.description:
When enabled, the goal game item will be sent to other compatible games as a gift,
and you can receive gifts from other players. This can be enabled during gameplay
using the client.

options.name: game_language
options.description: The language that the game should display. This does not have to match the given rom.

options.name: allow_bb
options.description:
Allow Boss Butch variants of bosses in Boss Shuffle.
Enabled: any boss placed will have a 50% chance of being the Boss Butch variant, including bosses not present
Enforced: all bosses will be their Boss Butch variant.
Boss Butch boss changes are only visual.

options.name: kirby_flavor_preset
options.description: The color of Kirby, from a list of presets.

options.name: gooey_flavor_preset
options.description: The color of Gooey, from a list of presets.

options.name: gooey_flavor
options.description:
A custom color for Gooey. To use a custom color, set the preset to Custom and then define a dict of keys from "1" to
"15", with their values being an HTML hex color.

options.name: music_shuffle
options.description:
None: default music will play
Shuffled: music will be shuffled amongst each other
Full: random music will play in each room
Note that certain songs will not be chosen in shuffled or full

options.name: virtual_console
options.description:
Adds the ability to enable 2 of the Virtual Console changes.
Flash Reduction: reduces the flashing during the Zero battle.

If toggled on, the player is required to have a certain keyblade to open chests in certain worlds.

TT   - Lionheart

options.name: keyblade_stats
options.description:
Determines whether Keyblade stats should be randomized.

Randomize: Randomly generates stats for each keyblade between the defined minimums and maximums.

Shuffle: Shuffles the stats of the vanilla keyblades amongst each other.

Vanilla: Keyblade stats are unchanged.

options.description:
Determines how much Orichalcum, one of the two synthesis items, is in the item pool.

You need 17 to synth every recipe that requires it.

options.name: orichalcum_price
options.description: Determines the cost of Orichalcum in each shop.

options.name: mythril_in_pool

Determines how much Mythril, one of the two synthesis items, is in the item pool.

You need 16 to synth every recipe that requires it.

options.name: mythril_price
options.description: Determines the cost of Mythril in each shop.

options.name: randomize_ap_costs
options.description:
Off: No randomization
Shuffle: Ability AP Costs will be shuffled amongst themselves.

Randomize: Ability AP Costs will be randomized to the specified max and min.

Distribute: Ability AP Costs will totalled and re-distributed randomly between the specified max and min.

options.name: max_ap_cost
options.description: If Randomize AP Costs is set to Randomize or Distribute, this defined the max AP cost an ability can have.

options.name: min_ap_cost
options.description: If Randomize AP Costs is set to Randomize or Distribute, this defined the min AP cost an ability can have.

options.name: starting_worlds
options.description:
Number of random worlds to start with in addition to Traverse Town, which is always available.

Will only consider Atlantica if toggled, and will only consider End of the World if its unlock is set to "Item".

These are given by the server, and are received after connection.

options.name: starting_tools
options.description:
Determines whether you start with Scan and Dodge Roll.

These are given by the server, and are received after connection.

options.name: randomize_puppies
options.description:
If OFF, the "Puppy" item is worth 3 puppies and puppies are placed in vanilla locations.

If ON, the "Puppy" item is worth an amount of puppies defined by "Puppy Value", and are shuffled randomly.

options.name: puppy_value
options.description: Determines how many dalmatian puppies are given when a puppy item is found.

options.name: interact_in_battle
options.description: Allow Sora to talk to people, examine objects, and open chests in battle.

options.name: logic_difficulty
options.description:
Determines what the randomizer logic may expect you to do to reach certain locations.

Beginner: Logic only expects what would be the natural solution in vanilla gameplay or similar, as well as a guarantee of tools for boss fights.

Normal: Logic expects some clever use of abilities, exploration of options, and competent combat ability; generally does not require advanced knowledge.

Proud: Logic expects advanced knowledge of tricks and obscure interactions, such as using Combo Master, Dumbo, and other unusual methods to reach locations.

Minimal: Logic expects the bare minimum to get to locations; may require extensive grinding, beating fights with no tools, and performing very difficult or tedious tricks.

options.name: extra_shared_abilities
options.description: If on, adds extra shared abilities to the pool.  These can stack, so multiple high jumps make you jump higher and multiple glides make you superglide faster.

options.name: stacking_world_items
options.description:
Multiple world items give you the world's associated key item.

WL - Footprints

OC - Entry Pass

DJ - Slides

HT - Forget-Me-Not and Jack-In-The-Box

HB - Theon Vol. 6

Adds an extra world to the pool for each that has a key item (WL, OC, DJ, HT, HB).

Forces Halloween Town Key Item Bundle ON.

options.name: halloween_town_key_item_bundle
options.description:
Obtaining the Forget-Me-Not automatically gives Jack-in-the-Box as well.

Removes Jack-in-the-Box from the pool.

options.name: exp_zero_in_pool
options.description: If on, adds EXP Zero ability to the item pool.  This is redundant if you are planning on playing on Proud.

options.name: randomize_party_member_starting_accessories
options.description:
If on, the 10 accessories that some party members (Aladdin, Ariel, Jack, Peter Pan, Beast) start with are randomized.

10 random accessories will be distributed amongst any party member aside from Sora in their starting equipment.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
If Sora is KO'ed, the other players with "Death Link" on will also be KO'ed.
The opposite is also true.

options.name: donald_death_link
options.description: If Donald is KO'ed, so is Sora.  If Death Link is toggled on in your client, this will send a death to everyone who enabled death link.

options.name: goofy_death_link
options.description: If Goofy is KO'ed, so is Sora.  If Death Link is toggled on in your client, this will send a death to everyone who enabled death link.

options.name: remote_items
options.description:
Determines if items can be placed on locations in your own world in such a way that will force them to be remote items.

Off: When your items are placed in your world, they can only be placed in locations that they can be acquired without server connection (stats on levels, items in chests, etc).

Allow: When your items are placed in your world, items that normally can't be placed in a location in-game are simply made remote (abilities on static events, etc).

Full: All items are remote.  Use this when doing something like a co-op seed.

options.name: shorten_go_mode
options.description: If on, the player warps to the final cutscene after defeating Ansem 1 > Darkside > Ansem 2, skipping World of Chaos.

options.name: one_hp
options.description: If on, forces Sora's max HP to 1 and removes the low health warning sound.

options.name: four_by_three
options.description: If on, changes the aspect ratio to 4 by 3.

options.name: auto_attack
options.description: If on, you can combo by holding confirm.

options.name: beep_hack
options.description: If on, removes low health warning sound.  Works up to max health of 41.

options.name: consistent_finishers
options.description: If on, 30% chance finishers are now 100% chance.

options.name: early_skip
options.description: If on, allows skipping cutscenes immediately that normally take time to be able to skip.

options.name: fast_camera
options.description: If on, speeds up camera movement and camera centering.

options.name: faster_animations
options.description: If on, speeds up animations during which you can't play.

options.name: unlock_0_volume
options.description: If on, volume 1 mutes the audio channel.

options.name: unskippable
options.description: If on, makes unskippable cutscenes skippable.

options.name: auto_save
options.description:
If on, enables auto saving.

Press L1+L2+R1+R2+D-Pad Left to instantly load continue state.

Press L1+L2+R1+R2+D-Pad Right to instantly load autosave.

options.name: warp_anywhere
options.description:
If on, enables the player to warp at any time, even when not at a save point.

Press L1+L2+R2+Select to open the Save/Warp menu at any time.

options.name: LevelDepth
options.description:
Determines How many locations you want on levels

Level 50: 23 checks spread through 50 levels.
Level 99: 23 checks spread through 99 levels.

Level 50 sanity: 49 checks spread through 50 levels.
Level 99 sanity: 98 checks spread through 99 levels.

Level 1: no checks on levels(checks are replaced with stats)

I.E. get three proofs+kill final Xemnas

options.name: FightLogic
options.description:
The level of logic to use when determining what fights in each KH2 world are beatable.

Easy: For Players not very comfortable doing things without a lot of tools.

Normal: For Players somewhat comfortable doing fights with some of the tools.

Hard: For Players comfortable doing fights with almost no tools.

options.name: FinalFormLogic
options.description:
Determines forcing final form logic

No Light and Darkness: Light and Darkness is not in logic.
Light And Darkness: Final Forcing with light and darkness is in logic.
Just a Form: All that requires final forcing is another form.

No Visit Locking: Start with all 25 visit locking items.


Second Visit Locking: Start with 13 visit locking items for every first visit.


First and Second Visit Locking: One item for First Visit Two For Second Visit

options.name: RandomVisitLockingItem
options.description: Start with random amount of visit locking items.

options.description:

No Cups: All Cups are placed into Excluded Locations.
Cups: Hades Paradox Cup is placed into Excluded Locations
Cups and Hades Paradox: Has Every Cup On.

options.name: SummonLevelLocationToggle
options.description: Toggle Summon levels to have locations.

options.name: AtlanticaToggle
options.description: Atlantica Toggle

options.name: CorSkipToggle
options.description:
Toggle for Cor skip.

Tools depend on which difficulty was chosen on Fight Difficulty.

Toggle does not negate fight logic but is an alternative.

Full Cor Skip is also affected by this Toggle.

options.name: CustomItemPoolQuantity
options.description: Add more of an item into the itempool. Note: You cannot take out items from the pool.

options.name: logic
options.description:
Affects where items are allowed to be placed.

**Normal:** Playable without using any tricks or glitches. Can require
knowledge from a vanilla playthrough, such as how to open Color Dungeon.

**Hard:** More advanced techniques may be required, but glitches are not.
Examples include tricky jumps, killing enemies with only pots.

**Glitched:** Advanced glitches and techniques may be required, but
extremely difficult or tedious tricks are not required. Examples include
Bomb Triggers, Super Jumps and Jesus Jumps.

**Hell:** Obscure knowledge and hard techniques may be required. Examples
include featherless jumping with boots and/or hookshot, sequential pit
buffers and unclipped superjumps. Things in here can be extremely hard to do
or very time consuming.

options.name: goal
options.description:
The Goal of the game.

**Instruments:** The Wind Fish's Egg will only open if you have the required
number of Instruments of the Sirens, and play the Ballad of the Wind Fish.

**Seashells:** The Egg will open when you bring 20 seashells. The Ballad and
Ocarina are not needed.

**Open:** The Egg will start pre-opened.

options.name: instrument_count
options.description: Sets the number of instruments required to open the Egg.

options.name: stealing
options.description: Puts stealing from the shop in logic if the player has a sword.

options.name: in_game_hints
options.description:
When enabled, owl statues and library books may indicate the location of
your items in the multiworld.

options.name: tarins_gift
options.description:
**Local Progression:** Forces Tarin's gift to be an item that immediately
opens up local checks. Has little effect in single player games, and isn't
always necessary with randomized entrances.

**Bush Breaker:** Forces Tarin's gift to be an item that can destroy bushes.

**Any Item:** Tarin's gift can be any item for any world

options.name: hard_mode
options.description:
**Oracle:** Less iframes and health from drops. Bombs damage yourself. Water
damages you without flippers. No pieces of power or acorns.

**Hero:** Switch version hero mode, double damage, no heart/fairy drops.

**OHKO:** You die on a single hit, always.

options.name: trendy_game
options.description:
**Easy:** All of the items hold still for you.

**Normal:** The vanilla behavior.

**Hard:** The trade item also moves.

**Harder:** The items move faster.

**Hardest:** The items move diagonally.

**Impossible:** The items move impossibly fast, may scroll on and off the
screen.

options.name: overworld
options.description:
**Open Mabe:** Replaces rock on the east side of Mabe Village with bushes,
allowing access to Ukuku Prairie without Power Bracelet.

options.name: warps
options.description:
**Improved:** Adds remake style warp screen to the game. Choose your warp
destination on the map after jumping in a portal and press *B* to select.

**Improved Additional:** Improved warps, and adds a warp point at Crazy
Tracy's house (the Mambo teleport spot) and Eagle's Tower.

options.name: experimental_dungeon_shuffle
options.description: Randomizes dungeon entrances with each other.

options.name: experimental_entrance_shuffle
options.description:
Randomizes where overworld entrances lead.

**Simple:** Single-entrance caves/houses that have items are shuffled
amongst each other.

If *Dungeon Shuffle* is enabled, then dungeons will be shuffled with all the
non-connector entrances in the pool. Note, some entrances can lead into water, use
the warp-to-home from the save&quit menu to escape this.

options.name: shuffle_instruments
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

**Vanilla:** The item will be in its vanilla location in your world.

options.name: shuffle_nightmare_keys
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.name: shuffle_small_keys
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.name: shuffle_maps
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.name: shuffle_compasses
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.name: shuffle_stone_beaks
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.name: tradequest
options.description:
Trade quest items are randomized. Each NPC takes its normal trade quest
item and gives a randomized item in return.

options.name: rooster
options.description:
Adds the rooster to the item pool. If disabled, the overworld will be
modified so that any location requiring the rooster is accessible by other
means.

options.name: stabilize_item_pool
options.description:
By default, some rupees in the item pool are randomly swapped with bombs,
arrows, powders, or capacity upgrades. This set of items is also used as
filler. This option disables that swapping and makes *Nothing* the filler
item.

options.name: nag_messages
options.description:
Controls if nag messages are shown when rocks and crystals are touched.
Useful for glitches, annoying for everything else.

options.name: quickswap
options.description: Instead of opening the map, the *SELECT* button swaps the top item of your inventory on to your *A* or *B* button.

options.name: boots_controls
options.description:
Adds an additional button to activate Pegasus Boots (does nothing if you
haven't picked up your boots!)

**Vanilla:** Nothing changes, you have to equip the boots to use them.

**Bracelet:** Holding down the button for the bracelet also activates boots
(somewhat like Link to the Past).

**Press A:** Holding down A activates boots.

**Press B:** Holding down B activates boots.

options.name: foreign_item_icons
options.description:
Choose how to display foreign items.

**Guess By Name:** Foreign items can look like any Link's Awakening item.

**Indicate Progression:** Foreign items are either a Piece of Power
(progression) or Guardian Acorn (non-progression).

options.name: gfxmod
options.description: If enabled, the patcher will prompt the user for a modification file to change sprites in the game and optionally some text.

options.name: link_palette
options.description:
Sets Link's palette.

A-D are color palettes usually used during the damage animation and can
change based on where you are.

options.name: palette
options.description:
Sets the palette for the game.

Note: A few places aren't patched, such as the menu and a few color dungeon
tiles.

**Normal:** The vanilla palette.

**1-Bit:** One bit of color per channel.

**2-Bit:** Two bits of color per channel.

**Greyscale:** Shades of grey.

**Pink:** Aesthetic.

**Inverted:** Inverted.

options.name: ap_title_screen
options.description: Enables AP specific title screen and disables the intro cutscene.

options.name: text_shuffle
options.description: Shuffles all text in the game.

options.name: text_mode
options.description: **Fast:** Makes text appear twice as fast.

options.name: music
options.description:
**Vanilla:** Regular Music

**Shuffled:** Shuffled Music

**Off:** No music

options.name: music_change_condition
options.description:
Controls how the music changes.

**Sword:** When you pick up a sword, the music changes.

**Always:** You always have the post-sword music.

options.name: low_hp_beep
options.description: Slows or disables the low health beeping sound.

options.name: no_flash
options.description:
Remove the flashing light effects from Mamu, shopkeeper and MadBatter.
Useful for capture cards and people that are sensitive to these things.

landstalker.game: Landstalker - The Treasures of King Nole

schema.game: Landstalker - The Treasures of King Nole

options.name: goal
options.description:
The goal to accomplish in order to complete the seed.
- Beat Gola: beat the usual final boss (same as vanilla)
- Reach Kazalt: find the jewels and take the teleporter to Kazalt
- Beat Dark Nole: the door to King Nole's fight brings you into a final dungeon with an absurdly hard boss you have
    to beat to win the game

options.name: spawn_region
options.description:
List of spawn locations that can be picked by the randomizer.
It is advised to keep Massan as your spawn location for your first few seeds.
Picking a late-game location can make the seed significantly harder, both for logic and combat.

options.name: jewel_count
options.description: Determines the number of jewels to find to be able to reach Kazalt.

options.name: progressive_armors
options.description:
When obtaining an armor, you get the next armor tier instead of getting the specific armor tier that was
placed here by randomization. Enabling this provides a smoother progression.

options.name: use_record_book
options.description:
Gives a Record Book item in starting inventory, allowing to save the game anywhere.
This makes the game significantly less frustrating and enables interesting save-scumming strategies in some places.

options.name: use_spell_book
options.description:
Gives a Spell Book item in starting inventory, allowing to warp back to the starting location at any time.
This prevents any kind of softlock and makes the world easier to explore.

options.name: shop_prices_factor
options.description:
Applies a percentage factor on all prices in shops. Having higher prices can lead to a bit of gold farming, which
can make seeds longer but also sometimes more frustrating.

options.name: combat_difficulty
options.description:
Determines the overall combat difficulty in the game by modifying both monsters HP & damage.
- Peaceful: 50% HP & damage
- Easy: 75% HP & damage
- Normal: 100% HP & damage
- Hard: 140% HP & damage
- Insane: 200% HP & damage

options.name: teleport_tree_requirements
options.description:
Determines the requirements to be able to use a teleport tree pair.
- None: All teleport trees are available right from the start
- Clear Tibor: Tibor needs to be cleared before unlocking any tree
- Visit Trees: Both trees from a tree pair need to be visited to teleport between them
Vanilla behavior is "Clear Tibor And Visit Trees"

options.name: shuffle_trees
options.description: If enabled, all teleportation trees will be shuffled into new pairs.

options.name: ensure_ekeeke_in_shops
options.description:
Ensures an EkeEke will always be for sale in one shop per region in the game.
Disabling this can lead to frustrating situations where you cannot refill your health items and might get locked.

options.name: remove_gumi_boulder
options.description:
Removes the boulder between Gumi and Ryuma, which is usually a one-way path.
This makes the vanilla early game (Massan, Gumi...) more easily accessible when starting outside it.

options.name: allow_whistle_usage_behind_trees
options.description:
In Greenmaze, Einstein Whistle can only be used to call Cutter from the intended side by default.
Enabling this allows using Einstein Whistle from both sides of the magic trees.
This is only useful in seeds starting in the "waterfall" spawn region or where teleportation trees are made open from the start.

options.name: handle_damage_boosting_in_logic
options.description:
Adds damage boosting as a logical rule, removing any requirements involving Iron Boots or Fireproof Boots.
Who doesn't like walking on spikes and lava?

options.name: handle_enemy_jumping_in_logic
options.description:
Adds jumping on enemies' heads as a logical rule.
This gives access to Mountainous Area from Lake Shrine sector and to the cliff chest behind a magic tree near Mir Tower.
These tricks not being easy, you should leave this disabled until practiced.

options.name: handle_tree_cutting_glitch_in_logic
options.description:
Adds tree-cutting glitch as a logical rule, enabling access to both chests behind magic trees in Mir Tower Sector
without having Axe Magic.

options.name: hint_count
options.description: Determines the number of Foxy NPCs that will be scattered across the world, giving various types of hints

options.name: revive_using_ekeeke
options.description:
In the vanilla game, when you die, you are automatically revived by Friday using an EkeEke.
This setting allows disabling this feature, making the game extremely harder.
USE WITH CAUTION!

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: shuffle_doors
options.description:
This option specifies how doors open.

- **None:** Doors in the game will open the way they do in vanilla.
- **Panels:** Doors still open as in vanilla, but the panels that open the
  doors will be locked, and an item will be required to unlock the panels.
- **Doors:** the doors themselves are locked behind items, and will open
  automatically without needing to solve a panel once the key is obtained.

options.name: group_doors
options.description:
By default, door shuffle in either panels or doors mode will create individual keys for every panel or door to be locked.

When group doors is on, some panels and doors are sorted into logical groups, which are opened together by receiving an item.

options.name: location_checks
options.description:
Determines what locations are available.

- **Normal:** There will be a location check for each panel set that would
  ordinarily open a door, as well as for achievement panels and a small
  handful of other panels.
- **Reduced:** Many of the locations that are associated with opening doors
  are removed.
- **Insanity:** Every individual panel in the game is a location check.

options.name: shuffle_colors
options.description:
If on, an item is added to the pool for every puzzle color (besides White).

You will need to unlock the requisite colors in order to be able to solve
puzzles of that color.

options.name: shuffle_panels
options.description:
Determines how panel puzzles are randomized.

- **None:** Most panels remain the same as in the base game. Note that there are
  some panels (in particular, in Starting Room and Second Room) that are changed
  by the randomizer even when panel shuffle is disabled.
- **Rearrange:** The puzzles are the same as the ones in the base game, but are
  placed in different areas.

More options for puzzle randomization are planned in the future.

options.name: shuffle_paintings
options.description: If on, the destination, location, and appearance of the painting warps in the game will be randomized.

options.name: victory_condition
options.description:
Change the victory condition.

- **The End:** the goal is to solve THE END at the top of the tower.
- **The Master:** The goal is to solve THE MASTER at the top of the tower,
  after getting the number of achievements specified in the Mastery
  Achievements option.
- **Level 2:** The goal is to solve LEVEL 2 in the second room, after
  solving the number of panels specified in the Level 2 Requirement option.
- **Pilgrimage:** The goal is to solve PILGRIM in the Pilgrim Antechamber,
  typically after performing a Pilgrimage.

options.name: early_color_hallways
options.description:
When on, a painting warp to the color hallways area will appear in the starting room.

This lets you avoid being trapped in the starting room for long periods of
time when door shuffle is on.

options.name: shuffle_postgame
options.description: When off, locations that could not be reached without also reaching your victory condition are removed.

options.name: death_link
options.description: If on: Whenever another player on death link dies, you will be returned to the starting room.

options.name: enable_pilgrimage
options.description:
Determines how the pilgrimage works.

- **On:** You are required to complete a pilgrimage in order to access the
  Pilgrim Antechamber.
- **Off:** The pilgrimage will be deactivated, and the sun painting will be
  added to the pool, even if door shuffle is off.

options.name: pilgrimage_allows_roof_access
options.description:
If on, you may use the Crossroads roof access during a pilgrimage (and you may be expected to do so).

Otherwise, pilgrimage will be deactivated when going up the stairs.

options.name: pilgrimage_allows_paintings
options.description:
If on, you may use paintings during a pilgrimage (and you may be expected to do so).

Otherwise, pilgrimage will be deactivated when going through a painting.

options.name: sunwarp_access
options.description:
Determines how access to sunwarps works.

- **Normal:** All sunwarps are enabled from the start.
- **Disabled:** All sunwarps are disabled. Pilgrimage must be disabled when
  this is used.
- **Unlock:** Sunwarps start off disabled, and all six activate once you
  receive an item.
- **Individual:** Sunwarps start off disabled, and each has a corresponding
  item that unlocks it.
- **Progressive:** Sunwarps start off disabled, and they unlock in order
  using a progressive item.

options.name: shuffle_sunwarps
options.description: If on, the pairing and ordering of the sunwarps in the game will be randomized.

options.name: progressive_orange_tower
options.description:
When "Shuffle Doors" is on doors mode, this setting governs the manner in which the Orange Tower floors open up.

- **Off:** There is an item for each floor of the tower, and each floor's
  item is the only one needed to access that floor.
- **On:** There are six progressive items, which open up the tower from the
  bottom floor upward.

options.name: progressive_colorful
options.description:
When "Shuffle Doors" is on either panels or doors mode and "Group Doors" is off, this setting governs the manner in which The Colorful opens up.

- **Off:** There is an item for each room of The Colorful, meaning that
  random rooms in the middle of the sequence can open up without giving you
  access to them.
- **On:** There are ten progressive items, which open up the sequence from
  White forward.

options.name: mastery_achievements
options.description:
The number of achievements required to unlock THE MASTER.

- In the base game, 21 achievements are needed.
- If you include The Scientific and The Unchallenged, which are in the base
  game but are not counted for mastery, 23 would be required.
- If you include the custom achievement (The Wanderer), 24 would be
  required.

options.name: level_2_requirement
options.description:
The number of panel solves required to unlock LEVEL 2.

In the base game, 223 are needed. Note that this count includes ANOTHER TRY.
When set to 1, the panel hunt is disabled, and you can access LEVEL 2 for
free.

options.name: trap_percentage
options.description: Replaces junk items with traps, at the specified rate.

options.name: trap_weights
options.description:
Specify the distribution of traps that should be placed into the pool.

If you don't want a specific type of trap, set the weight to zero.

options.name: speed_boost_mode
options.description:
If on, the player's default speed is halved, as if affected by a Slowness Trap. Speed Boosts are added to
the item pool, which temporarily return the player to normal speed. Slowness Traps are removed from the pool.

options.name: puzzle_skip_percentage
options.description: Replaces junk items with puzzle skips, at the specified rate.

options.name: blue_chest_chance
options.description:
The chance of a chest being a blue chest.

It is given in units of 1/256, i.e., a value of 25 corresponds to 25/256 ~ 9.77%.
If you increase the blue chest chance, then the red chest chance is decreased in return.
Supported values: 5 – 75
Default value: 25 (five times as much as in an unmodified game)

options.name: blue_chest_count
options.description:
The number of blue chest items that will be in your item pool.

The number of blue chests in your world that count as multiworld location checks will be equal this amount plus one
more for each party member or capsule monster if you have shuffle_party_members/shuffle_capsule_monsters enabled.
(You will still encounter blue chests in your world after all the multiworld location checks have been exhausted,
but these chests will then generate items for yourself only.)
Supported values: 10 – 100
Default value: 25

options.name: boss
options.description:
Which boss to fight on the final floor.

Supported values:
lizard_man, big_catfish, regal_goblin, follower_x2, camu, tarantula, pierre, daniele, gades_a, mummy_x4, troll_x3,
gades_b, idura_a, lion_x2, idura_b, idura_c, rogue_flower, soldier_x4, gargoyle_x4, venge_ghost, white_dragon_x3,
fire_dragon, ghost_ship, tank, gades_c, amon, erim, daos, egg_dragon, master
random-low — select a random regular boss, from lizard_man to troll_x3
random-middle — select a random regular boss, from idura_a to gargoyle_x4
random-high — select a random regular boss, from venge_ghost to tank
random-sinistral — select a random Sinistral boss
Default value: master (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: capsule_cravings_jp_style
options.description:
Make capsule monster cravings behave as in the Japanese version.

In the US version, the data that determines which items a capsule monster can request is a mess.
It allows only for a very limited selection of items to be requested, and the quality of the selected item is almost
always either too low or too high (compared to the capsule monsters current quality preference). This means that,
if fed, the requested item will either be rejected by the capsule monster or lead to an unreasonable increase of the
quality preference, making further feeding more difficult.
This setting provides a fix for the bug described above.
If enabled, the capsule monster feeding behavior will be changed to behave analogous to the JP (and EU) version.
This means that requests become more varied, while the requested item will be guaranteed to be of the same quality
as the capsule monsters current preference. Thus, it can no longer happen that the capsule monster dislikes eating
the very item it just requested.
Supported values: false, true
Default value: false (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: capsule_starting_form
options.description:
The starting form of your capsule monsters.

Supported values: 1 – 4, m
Default value: 1 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: capsule_starting_level
options.description:
The starting level of your capsule monsters.

Can be set to the special value party_starting_level to make it the same value as the party_starting_level option.
Supported values: 1 – 99, party_starting_level
Default value: 1 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: crowded_floor_chance
options.description:
The chance of a floor being a crowded floor.

It is given in units of 1/256, i.e., a value of 16 corresponds to 16/256 = 6.25%.
A crowded floor is a floor where most of the chests are grouped in one room together with many enemies.
Supported values: 0 – 255
Default value: 16 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: custom_item_pool
options.description:
Customize your multiworld item pool.

Using this option you can place any cave item in your multiworld item pool. (By default, the pool is filled with
blue chest items.) Here you can add any valid item from the Lufia II Ancient Cave section of the datapackage
(see https://archipelago.gg/datapackage). The value of this option has to be a mapping of item name to count,
e.g., to add two Deadly rods and one Dekar Blade: {Deadly rod: 2, Dekar blade: 1}
The maximum total amount of custom items you can place is limited by the chosen blue_chest_count; any remaining,
non-customized space in the pool will be occupied by random blue chest items.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: default_capsule
options.description:
Preselect the active capsule monster.

(Only has an effect if shuffle_capsule_monsters is set to false.)
Supported values: jelze, flash, gusto, zeppy, darbi, sully, blaze
Default value: jelze

options.name: default_party
options.description:
Preselect the party lineup.

(Only has an effect if shuffle_party_members is set to false.)
Supported values:
Can be set to any valid combination of up to 4 party member initials, e.g.:
M — Maxim
DGMA — Dekar, Guy, Maxim, and Arty
MSTL — Maxim, Selan, Tia, and Lexis
random-2p — a random 2-person party
random-3p — a random 3-person party
random-4p — a random 4-person party
Default value: M

options.name: enemy_floor_numbers
options.description:
Change which enemy types are encountered at which floor numbers.

Supported values:
vanilla
    Ninja, e.g., is allowed to appear on the 3 floors B44-B46
shuffle — The existing enemy types are redistributed among nearby floors. Shifts by up to 6 floors are possible.
    Ninja, e.g., will be allowed to appear on exactly 3 consecutive floors somewhere from B38-B40 to B50-B52
randomize — For each floor, new enemy types are chosen randomly from the set usually possible on floors [-6, +6].
    Ninja, e.g., is among the various possible selections for any enemy slot affecting the floors from B38 to B52
Default value: vanilla (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: enemy_movement_patterns
options.description:
Change the movement patterns of enemies.

Supported values:
vanilla
shuffle_by_pattern — The existing movement patterns are redistributed among each other.
    Sprites that usually share a movement pattern will still share movement patterns after shuffling
randomize_by_pattern — For each movement pattern, a new one is chosen randomly from the set of existing patterns.
    Sprites that usually share a movement pattern will still share movement patterns after randomizing
shuffle_by_sprite — The existing movement patterns of sprites are redistributed among the enemy sprites.
    Sprites that usually share a movement pattern can end up with different movement patterns after shuffling
randomize_by_sprite — For each sprite, a new movement is chosen randomly from the set of existing patterns.
    Sprites that usually share a movement pattern can end up with different movement patterns after randomizing
singularity — All enemy sprites use the same, randomly selected movement pattern
Alternatively, you can directly specify an enemy name such as "Red Jelly" as the value of this option.
    In that case, the movement pattern usually associated with this sprite will be used by all enemy sprites
Default value: vanilla (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: enemy_sprites
options.description:
Change the appearance of enemies.

Supported values:
vanilla
shuffle — The existing sprites are redistributed among the enemy types.
    This means that, after shuffling, exactly 1 enemy type will be dressing up as the "Red Jelly" sprite
randomize — For each enemy type, a new sprite is chosen randomly from the set of existing sprites.
    This means that, after randomizing, any number of enemy types could end up using the "Red Jelly" sprite
singularity — All enemies use the same, randomly selected sprite
Alternatively, you can directly specify an enemy name such as "Red Jelly" as the value of this option.
    In this case, the sprite usually associated with that enemy will be used by all enemies
Default value: vanilla (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: exp_modifier
options.description:
Percentage modifier for EXP gained from enemies.

Supported values: 100 – 500
Default value: 100 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: final_floor
options.description:
The final floor, where the boss resides.

Supported values: 2 – 99
Default value: 99 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: gear_variety_after_b9
options.description:
Fixes a bug that prevents various gear from appearing after B9.

Due to an overflow bug in the game, the distribution of red chest gear is impaired after B9.
Starting with B10, the number of items available from red chests is severely limited, meaning that red chests will
no longer contain any shields, headgear, rings, or jewels (and the selection of body armor is reduced as well).
This setting provides a fix for the bug described above.
If enabled, red chests beyond B9 will continue to produce shields, headgear, rings, and jewels as intended,
while the odds of finding body armor in red chests are decreased as a result.
The distributions of red chest weapons, spells, and consumables as well as blue chests are unaffected.
Supported values: false, true
Default value: false (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: goal
options.description:
The objective you have to fulfill in order to complete the game.

Supported values:
boss — defeat the boss on the final floor
iris_treasure_hunt — gather the required number of Iris treasures and leave the cave
boss_iris_treasure_hunt — complete both the "boss" and the "iris_treasure_hunt" objective (in any order)
final_floor — merely reach the final floor
Default value: boss

options.name: gold_modifier
options.description:
Percentage modifier for gold gained from enemies.

Supported values: 25 – 400
Default value: 100 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: healing_floor_chance
options.description:
The chance of a floor having a healing tile hidden under a bush.

It is given in units of 1/256, i.e., a value of 16 corresponds to 16/256 = 6.25%.
Supported values: 0 – 255
Default value: 16 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: inactive_exp_gain
options.description:
The rate at which characters not currently in the active party gain EXP.

Supported values: disabled, half, full
Default value: disabled (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: initial_floor
options.description:
The initial floor, where you begin your journey.

(If this value isn't smaller than the value of final_floor, it will automatically be set to final_floor - 1)
Supported values: 1 – 98
Default value: 1 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: iris_floor_chance
options.description:
The chance of a floor being able to generate an Iris treasure.

It is given in units of 1/256, i.e., a value of 5 corresponds to 5/256 ~ 1.95%.
