The true chance of a floor holding an Iris treasure you need is usually lower than the chance specified here, e.g.,
if you have already found 8 of 9 Iris items then the chance of generating the last one is only 1/9 of this value.
Supported values: 5 – 255
Default value: 5 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: iris_treasures_required
options.description:
The number of Iris treasures required to complete the goal.

This setting only has an effect if the "iris_treasure_hunt" or "boss_iris_treasure_hunt" goal is active.
Supported values: 1 – 9
Default value: 9

options.name: master_hp
options.description:
The number of hit points of the Master

(Only has an effect if boss is set to master.)
Supported values: 1 – 9980
Default value: 9980 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: party_starting_level
options.description:
The starting level of your party members.

Supported values: 1 – 99
Default value: 1 (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: run_speed
options.description:
Modifies the game to allow you to move faster than normal when pressing the Y button.

Supported values: disabled, double, triple, quadruple
Default value: disabled (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: shop_interval
options.description:
Place shops after a certain number of floors.

E.g., if you set this to 5, then you will be given the opportunity to shop after completing B5, B10, B15, etc.,
whereas if you set it to 1, then there will be a shop after every single completed floor.
Shops will offer a random selection of wares; on deeper floors, more expensive items might appear.
You can customize the stock that can appear in shops using the shop_inventory option.
You can control how much gold you will be obtaining from enemies using the gold_multiplier option.
Supported values: disabled, 1 – 10
Default value: disabled (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: shop_inventory
options.description:
Determine the item types that can appear in shops.

The value of this option should be a mapping of item categories (or individual items) to weights (non-negative
integers), which are used as relative probabilities when it comes to including these things in shops. (The actual
contents of the generated shops are selected randomly and are subject to additional constraints such as more
expensive things being allowed only on later floors.)
Supported keys:
non_restorative — a selection of mostly non-restorative red chest consumables
restorative — all HP- or MP-restoring red chest consumables
blue_chest — all blue chest items
spell — all red chest spells
gear — all red chest armors, shields, headgear, rings, and rocks (this respects the gear_variety_after_b9 option,
    meaning that you will not encounter any shields, headgear, rings, or rocks in shops from B10 onward unless you
    also enabled that option)
weapon — all red chest weapons
Additionally, you can also add extra weights for any specific cave item. If you want your shops to have a
higher than normal chance of selling a Dekar blade, you can, e.g., add "Dekar blade: 5".
You can even forego the predefined categories entirely and design a custom shop pool from scratch by providing
separate weights for each item you want to include.
(Spells, however, cannot be weighted individually and are only available as part of the "spell" category.)
Default value: {spell: 30, gear: 45, weapon: 82}

options.name: shuffle_capsule_monsters
options.description:
Shuffle the capsule monsters into the multiworld.

Supported values:
false — all 7 capsule monsters are available in the menu and can be selected right away
true — you start without capsule monster; 7 new "items" are added to your pool and shuffled into the multiworld;
    when one of these items is found, the corresponding capsule monster is unlocked for you to use
Default value: false (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: shuffle_party_members
options.description:
Shuffle the party members into the multiworld.

Supported values:
false — all 6 optional party members are present in the cafe and can be recruited right away
true — only Maxim is available from the start; 6 new "items" are added to your pool and shuffled into the
    multiworld; when one of these items is found, the corresponding party member is unlocked for you to use.
    While cave diving, you can add or remove unlocked party members by using the character items from the inventory
Default value: false (same as in an unmodified game)

options.name: shuffle_golden_coins
options.description:
Vanilla: Golden Coins are received when defeating bosses.
Shuffle: Shuffle the Golden Coins into the item pool and make bosses location checks.
Mario Coin Fragment Hunt: You start with all Golden Coins except the Mario Coin, which has been fragmented into many pieces.
You will see a Golden Coin being received when defeating bosses regardless of whether you are actually getting a coin.

options.name: required_golden_coins
options.description: Number of Golden Coins required to enter Mario's Castle. Ignored on Mario Coin Fragment Hunt.

options.name: mario_coin_fragment_percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler items to be replaced with Mario Coin Fragments. Note that the Coinsanity and Coinsanity
Checks options will greatly impact the number of replaceable filler items.

options.name: mario_coin_fragments_required_percentage
options.description: Percentage of the Mario Coins in the item pool that are required to put the Mario Coin together.

options.name: coinsanity
options.description:
Shuffles the singular coins found freestanding and in question mark blocks into the item pool, and adds location
checks made by obtaining a sufficient number of coins in particular levels within a single playthrough.

options.name: coinsanity_checks
options.description:
Number of Coinsanity checks.
A higher number means more checks, and smaller coin amounts per coin item in the item pool.
If Accessibility is set to Full, auto-scroll levels may have a lower maximum count, which may lead to this
value being limited.

options.name: shuffle_midway_bells
options.description:
Shuffle Midway Bells into the item pool. You can always start at the beginning of a level after obtaining the
Midway Bell by holding SELECT while entering the level (until you load into the level).
The Midway Bells in levels will trigger location checks whether this option is on or not, but they will only
set the checkpoint if this is off, otherwise you must obtain the Midway Bell item from the item pool.

options.name: marios_castle_midway_bell
options.description: Adds a Midway Bell to the final stage, just before the Wario fight.

options.name: shuffle_pipe_traversal
options.description:
Single: Shuffle a Pipe Traversal item into the item pool, which is required to enter any pipes.
Split: Shuffle 4 Pipe Traversal items, one required for entering pipes from each direction.
Note that being unable to enter pipes is very limiting and affects nearly half of all levels.

options.name: auto_scroll_mode
options.description:
Always: Any auto scroll levels will always auto-scroll.
Global Trap Item: Auto scroll levels will only auto-scroll after obtaining the Auto Scroll trap item.
Level Trap Items: As with Trap Item, but there is a separate trap item for each auto scroll level.
Global Cancel Item: Auto Scroll levels will stop auto-scrolling after obtaining the Auto Scroll Cancel item.
Level Cancel Items: As with Cancel Item, but there is a separate cancel item for each auto scroll level.
Chaos: Each level will randomly always auto scroll, have an Auto Scroll Trap, or have an Auto Scroll Cancel item.
The effects of Trap and Cancel items are permanent! If Accessibility is not set to Full,
Traps may cause locations to become permanently unreachable.
With individual level items, the number of auto scroll levels may be limited by the available space in the item
pool.

options.name: auto_scroll_chances
options.description: Chance per eligible level to be made into an auto scroll level. Can also set to Vanilla to leave them unchanged.

options.name: difficulty_mode
options.description:
Play in normal or easy mode. You can also start in Normal Mode with an "upgrade" to Easy Mode in the item pool,
or start in Easy Mode with a Normal Mode "trap" in the item pool.

options.name: randomize_enemies
options.description: Randomize enemies throughout levels.

options.name: randomize_platforms
options.description: Randomize platforms throughout levels.

options.name: randomize_music
options.description: Randomize the music that plays in levels and overworld areas.

options.name: energy_link
options.description:
All extra lives beyond 1 are transferred into the server's shared EnergyLink storage. If you drop to 0,
1 will be replenished if there is sufficient energy stored.

options.name: goal
options.description: Which goal must be achieved to trigger completion.

options.name: include_psi_keys
options.description: Whether PSI Keys should be included in the multiworld pool. If not, they will be in their vanilla locations.

options.name: include_evolution_traps
options.description:
Whether evolution traps should be included in the multiworld pool.
If not, they will be activated by bosses, as in vanilla.

options.name: item_cache_cost
death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: shuffle_shards
options.description: Whether mega shards should be item locations.

options.name: traps
options.description: Whether traps should be included in the itempool.

options.name: shop_price
options.description: Percentage modifier for shuffled item prices in shops

options.name: shop_price_plan
options.description: Plan specific prices on shop slots. Supports weighting

options.name: early_meditation
options.description: Guarantees meditation will be found early

options.name: logic_level
options.description:
The level of logic to use when determining what locations in your world are accessible.

**Normal:** Can require damage boosts, but otherwise approachable for someone who has beaten the game.

**Hard:** Expects more knowledge and tighter execution.
Has leashing, normal clips and much tighter d-boosting in logic.

options.name: limited_movement
options.description: Removes either rope dart or wingsuit from the itempool. Forces logic to at least hard and accessibility to minimal.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Requirement to finish the game.
To win with the power seal hunt goal, you must enter the Music Box through the shop chest.

options.name: music_box
options.description: Whether the music box gauntlet needs to be done.

options.name: notes_needed
options.description:
How many notes need to be found in order to access the Music Box.
6 are always needed to enter, so this places the others in your start inventory.

options.name: total_seals
options.description: Number of power seals that exist in the item pool when power seal hunt is the goal.

options.name: percent_seals_required
options.description: Percentage of total seals required to open the shop chest.

options.name: available_portals
options.description:
Number of portals that are available from the start. Autumn Hills, Howling Grotto, and Glacial Peak are always
available. If portal outputs are not randomized, Searing Crags will also be available.

options.name: shuffle_portals
options.description:
Whether the portals lead to random places.
Entering a portal from its vanilla area will always lead to HQ, and will unlock it if relevant.
Supports plando.

**None:** Portals will take you where they're supposed to.

**Shops:** Portals can lead to any area except Music Box and Elemental Skylands, with each portal output guaranteed
to not overlap with another portal's. Will only put you at a portal or a shop.

**Checkpoints:** Like Shops except checkpoints without shops are also valid drop points.

**Anywhere:** Like Checkpoints except it's possible for multiple portals to output to the same map.

options.name: shuffle_transitions
options.description:
Whether the transitions between the levels should be randomized.
Supports plando.

**None:** Level transitions lead where they should.

**Coupled:** Returning through a transition will take you from whence you came.

**Decoupled:** Any level transition can take you to any other level transition.

options.name: portal_plando
options.description:
Plando connections to be used with portal shuffle.
Documentation on using this can be found in The Messenger plando guide.

options.name: coins
options.description: Add all coin blocks in the game to the location pool.

options.name: difficult_logic
options.description:
This adjusts the logic to be more difficult in a few areas,
allowing for the logic to account for players getting to certain areas in unintended ways.
Enable at your own risk, this is not an option made for beginners.

options.name: castle_skip
options.description:
Skip straight from the Entrance Hall to Bowletta in Bowser's Castle.
All Bowser's Castle locations will be removed from the location pool.

options.name: extra_pipes
options.description: Gives the player access to pipes 1, 3, 4, and 6 from the start.

options.name: skip_minecart
options.description:
Skip the minecart minigame that leads you through Hoohoo Mountain Base.
This will remove the 1 location in the minecart cave from the location pool.

options.name: disable_surf
options.description: Remove the surf minigame location from the location pool.

options.name: disable_harhalls_pants
options.description: This will remove the Harhall's Pants check from the pool.

options.name: block_visibility
options.description:
This makes any hidden blocks in the game into regular item blocks and vice versa.
Disabled: Hidden blocks will remain invisible.
Hidden Visible: Hidden blocks will turn visible to the player.
Blocks Invisible: All item blocks will turn invisible. Hidden blocks will also remain invisible.

options.name: chuckle_beans
options.description:
Choose how you want chuckle bean digspots to be randomized.
An amount of chuckle beans will be removed from the item pool,
equal to the amount of locations removed by the setting that you choose.
None: No chuckle bean digspots will be added into the location pool.
Only Visible: Only chuckle bean digspots clearly marked with an X will be added into the location pool.
All: All chuckle bean digspots will be added into the location pool.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Vanilla: Complete jokes end with the required items and defeat Birdo to unlock Bowser's Castle.

Emblem Hunt: Find the required number of Beanstar Emblems to gain access to Bowser's Castle.

options.name: emblems_required
options.description:
Number of Beanstar Emblems to collect to unlock Bowser's Castle.

If Goal is not Emblem Hunt, this does nothing.

options.name: emblems_amount
options.description:
Number of Beanstar Emblems that are in the pool.

If Goal is not Emblem Hunt, this does nothing.

options.name: music_options
options.description:
Choose if you want to randomize or disable music.
default: Music will be untouched.
randomize: Music will be randomized.
disable: All music will be disabled. No music will play throughout the entire game.

options.name: randomize_sounds
options.description: Randomizes every sound in the game, minus a select few that can softlock the game.

options.name: randomize_enemies
options.description:
Randomize all normal enemy encounters in the game.
If Bowser's castle skip is enabled, then enemies from Bowser's Castle will not be included.
Disabled: Enemies will not be randomized.
Vanilla Groups: Vanilla enemy groups will be shuffled with each other. Custom enemy groups will not be made.
Custom Groups: Custom enemy groups will be made and shuffled. Some enemy groups will only be semi-random,
including groups with flying enemies or pestnuts in them.

options.name: randomize_bosses
options.description:
Randomize all boss encounters in the game.
If Bowser's castle skip is enabled then bosses from Bowser's Castle will not be included.
Some bosses are not randomized due to flags, and story (such as the final boss).
Boss Only: Bosses will only be swapped with another boss.
Boss Normal: Bosses can be swapped with normal enemy encounters.

options.name: randomize_backgrounds
options.description: This randomizes the background image in battles.

options.name: scale_stats
options.description:
This scales enemy HP, POW, DEF, and XP to vanilla values.
This setting is intended for use with the Enemy Randomizer and is Recommended to turn on.
If you are not using the Enemy Randomizer the effects will be minimal.

options.name: xp_multiplier
options.description: This will multiply any XP you receive in battle by the chosen multiplier.

options.name: tattle_hp
options.description: This will display the enemies' current and max health while in battle.

options.name: mario_color
options.description: This changes the color of Mario's hat, as well as some key colors that are red including UI etc.

options.name: luigi_color
options.description: This changes the color of Luigi's hat, as well as some key colors that are green including UI etc.

options.name: mario_pants
options.description: This changes the color of Mario's trousers.

options.name: luigi_pants
options.description: This changes the color of Luigi's trousers.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: energy_link
options.description:
Enables EnergyLink support.
When enabled, pickups dropped from enemies are sent to the EnergyLink pool, and healing/weapon energy/1-Ups can
be requested from the EnergyLink pool.
Some of the energy sent to the pool will be lost on transfer.

options.name: starting_robot_master
options.description: The initial stage unlocked at the start.

options.name: consumables
options.description:
When enabled, e-tanks/1-ups/health/weapon energy will be added to the pool of items and included as checks.
E-Tanks and 1-Ups add 20 checks to the pool.
Weapon/Health Energy add 27 checks to the pool.

options.name: yoku_jumps
options.description:
When enabled, the player is expected to be able to perform the yoku block sequence in Heat Man's
stage without Item 2.

options.name: enable_lasers
options.description:
When enabled, the player is expected to complete (and acquire items within) the laser sections of Quick Man's
stage without the Time Stopper.

options.name: enemy_weakness
options.description: Randomizes the damage dealt to enemies by weapons. Friender will always take damage from the buster.

options.name: strict_weakness
options.description:
Only your starting Robot Master will take damage from the Mega Buster, the rest must be defeated with weapons.
Weapons that only do 1-3 damage to bosses no longer deal damage (aside from Alien).

options.name: random_weakness
options.description:
None: Bosses will have their regular weaknesses.
Shuffled: Weapon damage will be shuffled amongst the weapons, so Metal Blade may do Bubble Lead damage.
Time Stopper will deplete half of a random Robot Master's HP.
Randomized: Weapon damage will be fully randomized.

options.name: wily_5_requirement
options.description:
Change the number of Robot Masters that are required to be defeated for
the teleporter to the Wily Machine to appear.

options.name: plando_weakness
options.description:
Specify specific damage numbers for boss damage. Can be used even without strict/random weaknesses.
plando_weakness:
    Robot Master:
        Weapon: Damage

options.name: palette_shuffle
options.description:
Change the color of Mega Man and the Robot Masters.
None: The palettes are unchanged.
Shuffled: Palette colors are shuffled amongst the robot masters.
Randomized: Random (usually good) palettes are generated for each robot master.
Singularity: one palette is generated and used for all robot masters.
Supports custom palettes using HTML named colors in the
following format: Mega Buster-Lavender|Violet;randomized
The first value is the character whose palette you'd like to define, then separated by - is a set of 2 colors for
that character. separate every color with a pipe, and separate every character as well as the remaining shuffle with
a semicolon.

options.name: quickswap
options.description: When enabled, the player can quickswap through all received weapons by pressing Select.

options.name: reduce_flashing
options.description:
Reduce flashing seen in gameplay, such as the stage select and when defeating a Wily boss.
Virtual Console: increases length of most flashes, changes some flashes from white to a dark gray.
Minor: VC changes + decreasing the speed of Bubble/Metal Man stage animations.
Full: VC changes + further decreasing the brightness of most flashes and
disables stage animations for Metal/Bubble Man stages.

options.name: random_music
options.description:
Vanilla: music is unchanged
Shuffled: stage and certain menu music is shuffled.
Randomized: stage and certain menu music is randomly selected
None: no music will play

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: energy_link
options.description:
Enables EnergyLink support.
When enabled, pickups dropped from enemies are sent to the EnergyLink pool, and healing/weapon energy/1-Ups can
be requested from the EnergyLink pool.
Some of the energy sent to the pool will be lost on transfer.

options.name: starting_robot_master
options.description: The initial stage unlocked at the start.

options.name: consumables
options.description: When enabled, e-tanks/1-ups/health/weapon energy will be added to the pool of items and included as checks.

options.name: enemy_weakness
options.description: Randomizes the damage dealt to enemies by weapons. Certain enemies will always take damage from the buster.

options.name: strict_weakness
options.description:
Only your starting Robot Master will take damage from the Mega Buster, the rest must be defeated with weapons.
Weapons that only do 1-3 damage to bosses no longer deal damage (aside from Wily/Gamma).

options.name: random_weakness
options.description:
None: Bosses will have their regular weaknesses.
Shuffled: Weapon damage will be shuffled amongst the weapons, so Shadow Blade may do Top Spin damage.
Randomized: Weapon damage will be fully randomized.

options.name: wily_4_requirement
options.description:
Change the amount of Robot Masters that are required to be defeated for
the door to the Wily Machine to open.

options.name: plando_weakness
options.description:
Specify specific damage numbers for boss damage. Can be used even without strict/random weaknesses.
plando_weakness:
    Robot Master:
        Weapon: Damage

options.name: palette_shuffle
options.description:
Change the color of Mega Man and the Robot Masters.
None: The palettes are unchanged.
Shuffled: Palette colors are shuffled amongst the robot masters.
Randomized: Random (usually good) palettes are generated for each robot master.
Singularity: one palette is generated and used for all robot masters.
Supports custom palettes using HTML named colors in the
following format: Mega Buster-Lavender|Violet;randomized
The first value is the character whose palette you'd like to define, then separated by - is a set of 2 colors for
that character. separate every color with a pipe, and separate every character as well as the remaining shuffle with
a semicolon.

options.name: reduce_flashing
options.description: Reduce flashing seen in gameplay, such as in stages and when defeating certain bosses.

options.name: music_shuffle
options.description: Shuffle the music that plays in every stage

options.name: extra_ranks
options.description:
How many extra Undernet Ranks to add to the pool in place of filler items.
The more ranks there are, the faster the game will go.
Depending on your other options, you might not have enough filler items to replace.
If generation errors occur, consider reducing this value.

options.name: include_jobs
options.description: Whether Jobs can contain progression or useful items.

options.name: include_secret
options.description: Whether the Secret Area (including Serenade) can contain progression or useful items.

options.name: trade_quest_hinting
options.description:
Whether NPCs offering Chip Trades should show what item they provide.
None - NPCs will not provide any information on what item they will give
Partial - NPCs will state if an item is progression or not, but not the specific item
Full - NPCs will state what item they will give, providing an Archipelago Hint when doing so

options.name: starting_song_count
options.description: The number of songs that will be automatically unlocked at the start of a run.

options.name: additional_song_count
options.description:
The total number of songs that will be placed in the randomization pool.
- This does not count any starting songs or the goal song.
- The final song count may be lower due to other settings.

options.name: music_sheet_count_percentage
options.description:
Controls how many music sheets are added to the pool based on the number of songs, including starting songs.

Higher numbers leads to more consistent game lengths, but will cause individual music sheets to be less important.

options.name: music_sheet_win_count_percentage
options.description: The percentage of Music Sheets in the item pool that are needed to unlock the winning song.

options.name: dlc_packs
options.description:
Choose which DLC Packs will be included in the pool of chooseable songs.

Note: The [Just As Planned] DLC contains all [Muse Plus] songs.

options.name: streamer_mode_enabled
options.description:
In Muse Dash, an option named 'Streamer Mode' removes songs which may trigger copyright issues when streaming.

If this is enabled, only songs available under Streamer Mode will be available for randomization.

options.name: include_songs
options.description:
These songs will be guaranteed to show up within the seed.
- You must have the DLC enabled to play these songs.
- Difficulty options will not affect these songs.
- If there are too many included songs, this will act as a whitelist ignoring song difficulty.

options.name: exclude_songs
options.description:
These songs will be guaranteed to not show up within the seed.

Note: Does not affect songs within the "Include Songs" list.

options.name: goal_song
options.description:
One of the selected songs will be guaranteed to show up as the final Goal Song.
- You must have the DLC enabled to play these songs.
- If no songs are chosen, then the song will be randomly chosen from the available songs.

options.name: grade_needed
options.description:
Completing a song will require a grade of this value or higher in order to unlock items.
The grades are as follows:
- Silver S (SS): >= 95% accuracy
- Pink S (S): >= 90% accuracy
- A: >= 80% or a Full Combo
- B: >= 70%
- C: >= 60%

options.name: song_difficulty_mode
options.description:
Ensures that at any chosen song has at least 1 value falling within these values.
- Any: All songs are available
- Easy: 1, 2 or 3
- Medium: 4, 5
- Hard: 6, 7
- Expert: 8, 9
- Master: 10+
- Manual: Uses the provided minimum and maximum range.

options.name: song_difficulty_min
options.description:
Ensures that 1 difficulty has at least 1 this value or higher per song.

Note: Difficulty Mode must be set to Manual.

options.name: song_difficulty_max
options.description:
Ensures that 1 difficulty has at least 1 this value or lower per song.

Note: Difficulty Mode must be set to Manual.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: chosen_traps
options.description:
This controls the types of traps that can be added to the pool.
- Traps last the length of a song, or until you die.
- VFX Traps consist of visual effects that play over the song. (i.e. Grayscale.)
- SFX Traps consist of changing your sfx setting to one possibly more annoying sfx.

Note: SFX traps are only available if [Just as Planned] DLC songs are enabled.

options.name: trap_count_percentage
options.description: This controls how many traps to add into the pool, based the total number of songs.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

You can disable this or set it to give yourself a trap effect when another player dies in the in-game mod options.

options.name: bad_effects
options.description: Whether negative effects on the Noita world are added to the item pool.

options.name: victory_condition
options.description:
Greed is to get to the bottom, beat the boss, and win the game.
Pure is to get 11 orbs, grab the sampo, and bring it to the mountain altar.
Peaceful is to get all 33 orbs, grab the sampo, and bring it to the mountain altar.
Orbs will be added to the randomizer pool based on which victory condition you chose.
The base game orbs will not count towards these victory conditions.

options.name: path_option
options.description:
Choose where you would like Hidden Chest and Pedestal checks to be placed.
Main Path includes the main 7 biomes you typically go through to get to the final boss.
Side Path includes the Lukki Lair and Fungal Caverns. 9 biomes total.
Main World includes the full world (excluding parallel worlds). 15 biomes total.
Note: The Collapsed Mines have been combined into the Mines as the biome is tiny.

options.name: hidden_chests
options.description:
Number of hidden chest checks added to the applicable biomes.
Note: The number of hidden chests that spawn per run in each biome varies.
You are expected do multiple runs to get all of your checks.

options.name: pedestal_checks
options.description:
Number of checks that will spawn on pedestals in the applicable biomes.
Note: The number of pedestals that spawn per run in each biome varies.
You are expected do multiple runs to get all of your checks.

options.name: orbs_as_checks
options.description:
Decides whether finding the orbs that naturally spawn in the world count as checks.
The Main Path option includes only the Floating Island and Abyss Orb Room orbs.
The Side Path option includes the Main Path, Magical Temple, Lukki Lair, and Lava Lake orbs.
The Main World option includes all 11 orbs.

options.name: bosses_as_checks
options.description:
Makes bosses count as location checks. The boss only needs to die, you do not need the kill credit.
The Main Path option includes Gate Guardian, Suomuhauki, and Kolmisilmä.
The Side Path option includes the Main Path bosses, Sauvojen Tuntija, and Ylialkemisti.
The All Bosses option includes all 15 bosses.

options.name: extra_orbs
options.description:
Add extra orbs to your item pool, to prevent you from needing to wait as long for the last orb you need for your victory condition.
Extra orbs received past your victory condition's amount will be received as hearts instead.
Can be turned on for the Greed Ending goal, but will only really make it harder.

options.name: shop_price
options.description:
Reduce the costs of Archipelago items in shops.
By default, the price of Archipelago items matches the price of wands at that shop.

options.name: starting_area
options.description:
Which chunks are available at the start. The player may need to move through locked chunks to reach the starting
area, but any areas that require quests, skills, or coins are not available as a starting location.

"Any Bank" rolls a random region that contains a bank.
Chunksanity can start you in any chunk. Hope you like woodcutting!

options.name: brutal_grinds
options.description:
Whether to allow skill tasks without having reasonable access to the usual skill training path.
For example, if enabled, you could be forced to train smithing without an anvil purely by smelting bars,
or training fishing to high levels entirely on shrimp.

options.name: progressive_tasks
options.description:
Whether skill tasks should always be generated in order of easiest to hardest.
If enabled, you would not be assigned "Mine Gold" without also being assigned
"Mine Silver", "Mine Coal", and "Mine Iron". Enabling this will result in a generally shorter seed, but with
a lower variety of tasks.

options.name: enable_duds
options.description: Whether to include filler "Dud" items that serve no purpose but allow for more tasks in the pool.

options.name: dud_count
options.description: How many "Dud" items to include in the pool. This setting is ignored if "Enable Duds" is not included

options.name: enable_carepacks
options.description:
Whether or not to include useful "Care Pack" items that allow you to trade over specific items.
Note: Requires your account NOT to be an Ironman. Also, requires access to another account to trade over the items,
or gold to purchase off of the grand exchange.

options.name: max_combat_level
options.description:
The highest combat level of monster to possibly be assigned as a task.
If set to 0, no combat tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_combat_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Combat Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no combat tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: combat_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating combat tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_prayer_level
options.description:
The highest Prayer requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Prayer tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_prayer_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Prayer Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Prayer tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: prayer_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Prayer tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_magic_level
options.description:
The highest Magic requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Magic tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_magic_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Magic Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Magic tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: magic_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Magic tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_runecraft_level
options.description:
The highest Runecraft requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Runecraft tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_runecraft_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Runecraft Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Runecraft tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: runecraft_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Runecraft tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_crafting_level
options.description:
The highest Crafting requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Crafting tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_crafting_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Crafting Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Crafting tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: crafting_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Crafting tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_mining_level
options.description:
The highest Mining requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Mining tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_mining_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Mining Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Mining tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: mining_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Mining tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_smithing_level
options.description:
The highest Smithing requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Smithing tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_smithing_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Smithing Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Smithing tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: smithing_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Smithing tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_fishing_level
options.description:
The highest Fishing requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Fishing tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_fishing_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Fishing Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Fishing tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: fishing_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Fishing tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_cooking_level
options.description:
The highest Cooking requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Cooking tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_cooking_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Cooking Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Cooking tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: cooking_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Cooking tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_firemaking_level
options.description:
The highest Firemaking requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Firemaking tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_firemaking_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Firemaking Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Firemaking tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: firemaking_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Firemaking tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: max_woodcutting_level
options.description:
The highest Woodcutting requirement of any task generated.
If set to 0, no Woodcutting tasks will be generated.

options.name: max_woodcutting_tasks
options.description:
The maximum number of Woodcutting Tasks to possibly be assigned.
If set to 0, no Woodcutting tasks will be generated.
This only determines the maximum possible, fewer than the maximum could be assigned.

options.name: woodcutting_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating Woodcutting tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: minimum_general_tasks
options.description:
How many guaranteed general progression tasks to be assigned (total level, total XP, etc.).
General progression tasks will be used to fill out any holes caused by having fewer possible tasks than needed, so
there is no maximum.

options.name: general_task_weight
options.description:
How much to favor generating General tasks over other types of task.
Weights of all Task Types will be compared against each other, a task with 50 weight
is twice as likely to appear as one with 25.

options.name: location_balancing
options.description:
Location balancing affects the density of progression items found in your world relative to other worlds. This setting changes nothing for solo games.

- Disabled: Location density in your world can fluctuate greatly depending on the settings of other players. In extreme cases, your world may be entirely populated with filler items

- Compromise: Locations are balanced to a midpoint between "fair" and "natural"

- Full: Locations are balanced in an attempt to make the number of progression items sent out and received equal over the entire game

options.name: ramp_tricks
options.description: If enabled, generated games may require sequence breaks on the overworld map. This includes crossing small gaps and escaping out of bounds.

options.name: deathlink
options.description:
DeathLink is an opt-in feature for Multiworlds where individual death events are propagated to all games with DeathLink enabled.

- Disabled: Death will behave as it does in the original game.

- Death Only: A DeathLink broadcast will be sent every time a chef falls into a stage hazard. All local chefs will be killed when any one perishes.

- Death and Overcook: Same as above, but an additional broadcast will be sent whenever the kitchen catches on fire from burnt food.

options.name: shuffle_level_order
options.description: Shuffles the order of kitchens on the overworld map. Also draws from DLC maps.

options.name: include_dlcs
options.description: Which DLCs should be included when 'Shuffle Level Order' is enabled?'

options.name: include_horde_levels
options.description:
Includes "Horde Defense" levels in the pool of possible kitchens when Shuffle Level Order is enabled. Also adds
two horde-specific items into the item pool.

options.name: prep_levels
options.description:
Choose How "Prep Levels" are handled (levels where the timer does not start until the first order is served):

- Original: Prep Levels may appear

- Excluded: Prep Levels are excluded from the pool during level shuffling

- All You Can Eat: Prep Levels may appear, but the timer automatically starts. The star score requirements are also
adjusted to use the All You Can Eat World Record (if it exists)

options.name: kevin_levels
options.description: Includes the 8 Kevin level locations on the map as unlockables. Turn off to make games shorter.

options.name: fix_bugs
options.description:
Fixes Bugs Present in the base game:
- Double Serving Exploit
- Sink Bug
- Control Stick Cancel/Throw Bug
- Can't Throw Near Empty Burner Bug

options.name: shorter_level_duration
options.description:
Modifies level duration to be about 1/3rd shorter than in the original game, thus bringing the item discovery
pace in line with other popular Archipelago games.

Points required to earn stars are scaled accordingly. ("Boss Levels" which change scenery mid-game are not
affected.)

options.name: short_horde_levels
options.description:
Modifies horde levels to contain roughly 1/3rd fewer waves than in the original game.

The kitchen's health is scaled appropriately to preserve the same approximate difficulty.

options.name: always_preserve_cooking_progress
options.description:
Modifies the game to behave more like AYCE, where adding an item to an in-progress container doesn't reset the
entire progress bar.

options.name: always_serve_oldest_order
options.description:
Modifies the game so that serving an expired order doesn't target the ticket with the highest tip. This helps
players dig out of a broken tip combo faster.

options.name: display_leaderboard_scores
options.description:
Modifies the Overworld map to fetch and display the current world records for each level. Press number keys 1-4
to view leaderboard scores for that number of players.

options.name: stars_to_win
options.description:
Number of stars required to unlock 6-6.

Level purchase requirements between 1-1 and 6-6 will be spread between these two numbers. Using too high of a number
may result in more frequent generation failures, especially when horde levels are enabled.

options.name: star_threshold_scale
options.description:
How difficult should the third star for each level be on a scale of 1-100%, where 100% is the current world
record score and 45% is the average vanilla 4-star score.

options.name: logic_percent
options.description:
Sets the maximum percent similarity required for a check to be in logic.
Higher values are more difficult and items/locations will not be generated beyond this number.

options.name: goal_percent
options.description:
Sets the percent similarity required to achieve your goal.
If this number is higher than the value for logic percent,
reaching goal will be in logic upon obtaining all progression items.

options.name: half_percent_checks
options.description:
Sets the lowest percent at which locations will be created for each 0.5% of similarity.
Below this number, there will be a check every 1%.
Above this number, there will be a check every 0.5%.

options.name: quarter_percent_checks
options.description:
Sets the lowest percent at which locations will be created for each 0.25% of similarity.
This number will override Half Percent Checks if it is lower.

options.name: canvas_size_increment
options.description:
Sets the number of pixels the canvas will expand for each width/height item received.
Ensure an adequate number of locations are generated if setting this below 50.

options.name: starting_tool
options.description: Sets which tool (other than Magnifier) you will be able to use from the start.

options.name: trap_count
options.description: Sets the percentage of filler items to be replaced by random traps.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
If on, using the Undo or Clear Image functions will send a death to all other players with death link on.
Receiving a death will clear the image and reset the history.
This option also prevents Undo and Clear Image traps from being generated in the item pool.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Determines what your goal is to consider the game beaten.

- Champion: Become the champion and enter the hall of fame
- Steven: Defeat Steven in Meteor Falls
- Norman: Defeat Norman in Petalburg Gym
- Legendary Hunt: Defeat or catch legendary pokemon (or whatever was randomized into their encounters)

options.name: badges
options.description:
Adds Badges to the pool.

- Vanilla: Gym leaders give their own badge
- Shuffle: Gym leaders give a random badge
- Completely Random: Badges can be found anywhere

options.name: hms
options.description:
Adds HMs to the pool.

- Vanilla: HMs are at their vanilla locations
- Shuffle: HMs are shuffled among vanilla HM locations
- Completely Random: HMs can be found anywhere

options.name: key_items
options.description:
Adds most key items to the pool.

These are usually required to unlock a location or region (e.g. Devon Scope, Letter, Basement Key).

options.name: bikes
options.description: Adds the Mach Bike and Acro Bike to the pool.

options.name: event_tickets
options.description: Adds the event tickets to the pool, which let you access legendaries by sailing from Lilycove.

options.name: rods
options.description: Adds fishing rods to the pool.

options.name: overworld_items
options.description: Adds items on the ground with a Pokeball sprite to the pool.

options.name: hidden_items
options.description: Adds hidden items to the pool.

options.name: npc_gifts
options.description: Adds most gifts received from NPCs to the pool (not including key items or HMs).

options.name: berry_trees
options.description: Adds berry trees to the pool. Empty soil patches are converted to locations and contribute Sitrus Berries to the pool.

options.name: dexsanity
options.description:
Adding a "caught" pokedex entry gives you an item (catching, evolving, trading, etc.). Only wild encounters are considered logical access to a species.

Blacklisting wild encounters removes the dexsanity location.

Defeating gym leaders provides dex info, allowing you to see where on the map you can catch species you need.

Each pokedex entry adds a Poke Ball, Great Ball, or Ultra Ball to the pool.

Warning: This adds a lot of locations and will slow you down significantly.

options.name: dexsanity_encounter_types
options.description:
Determines which Dexsanity encounter areas are in logic.

Logic will only consider access to Pokemon at these encounter types, but they may still be found elsewhere.

options.name: trainersanity
options.description:
Defeating a trainer gives you an item.

Trainers are no longer missable. Trainers no longer give you money for winning. Each trainer adds a valuable item (Nugget, Stardust, etc.) to the pool.

Warning: This adds a lot of locations and will slow you down significantly.

options.name: item_pool_type
options.description:
Determines which non-progression items get put into the item pool.

- Shuffled: Item pool consists of shuffled vanilla items
- Diverse Balanced: Item pool consists of random items approximately proportioned according to what they're replacing
- Diverse: Item pool consists of uniformly random (non-unique) items

options.name: require_itemfinder
options.description: The Itemfinder is logically required to pick up hidden items.

options.name: require_flash
options.description: Determines whether HM05 Flash is logically required to navigate a dark cave.

options.name: elite_four_requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirements to challenge the elite four.

- Badges: Obtain some number of badges
- Gyms: Defeat some number of gyms

options.name: elite_four_count
options.description: Sets the number of badges/gyms required to challenge the elite four.

options.name: norman_requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirements to challenge the Petalburg Gym.

- Badges: Obtain some number of badges
- Gyms: Defeat some number of gym leaders

options.name: norman_count
options.description: Sets the number of badges/gyms required to challenge the Petalburg Gym.

options.name: legendary_hunt_catch
options.description:
Sets whether legendaries need to be caught to satisfy the Legendary Hunt win condition.

Defeated legendaries can be respawned by defeating the Elite 4.

options.name: legendary_hunt_count
options.description: Sets the number of legendaries that must be caught/defeated for the Legendary Hunt goal.

options.name: allowed_legendary_hunt_encounters
options.description:
Sets which legendary encounters can contribute to the Legendary Hunt goal.

Latias will always be at Southern Island. Latios will always be the roamer. The TV broadcast describing the roamer gives you "seen" info for Latios.

The braille puzzle in Sealed Chamber gives you "seen" info for Wailord and Relicanth. The move tutor in Fortree City always teaches Dig.

options.name: wild_pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes wild pokemon encounters (grass, caves, water, fishing).

Warning: Matching both base stats and type may severely limit the variety for certain pokemon.

- Vanilla: Wild encounters are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Wild pokemon are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Wild pokemon are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.name: wild_encounter_blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing in the wild when wild encounters are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "_Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary pokemon.

options.name: starters
options.description:
Randomizes the starter pokemon in Professor Birch's bag.

- Vanilla: Starters are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Starters are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Starters are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.name: starter_blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing as starters when starters are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "_Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary pokemon.

options.name: trainer_parties
options.description:
Randomizes the parties of all trainers.

Warning: Matching both base stats and type may severely limit the variety for certain pokemon.

- Vanilla: Parties are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Trainer pokemon are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Trainer pokemon are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.name: trainer_party_blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing in opponent trainers' parties if opponent parties are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "_Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary pokemon.

options.name: force_fully_evolved
options.description:
When an opponent uses a pokemon of the specified level or higher, restricts the species to only fully evolved pokemon.

Only applies when trainer parties are randomized.

Warning: Combining a low value with matched base stats may severely limit the variety for certain pokemon.

options.name: legendary_encounters
options.description:
Randomizes legendary encounters (Rayquaza, Regice, Latias, etc.). The roamer will always be Latios during legendary hunts.

- Vanilla: Legendary encounters are unchanged
- Shuffle: Legendary encounters are shuffled between each other
- Match Base Stats: Legendary encounters are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Legendary encounters are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.name: misc_pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes non-legendary static encounters. May grow to include other pokemon like trades or gifts.

- Vanilla: Species are unchanged
- Shuffle: Species are shuffled between each other
- Match Base Stats: Species are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Species are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.name: types
options.description:
Randomizes the type(s) of every pokemon. Each species will have the same number of types.

- Vanilla: Types are unchanged
- Shuffle: Types are shuffled globally for all species (e.g. every Water-type pokemon becomes Fire-type)
- Completely Random: Each species has its type(s) randomized
- Follow Evolutions: Types are randomized per evolution line instead of per species

options.name: abilities
options.description:
Randomizes abilities of every species. Each species will have the same number of abilities.

- Vanilla: Abilities are unchanged
- Completely Random: Each species has its abilities randomized
- Follow Evolutions: Abilities are randomized, but if a pokemon would normally retain its ability when evolving, the random ability will also be retained

options.name: ability_blacklist
options.description:
Prevent species from being given these abilities.

Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.

options.name: level_up_moves
options.description:
Randomizes the moves a pokemon learns when they reach a level where they would learn a move. Your starter is guaranteed to have a usable damaging move.

- Vanilla: Learnset is unchanged
- Randomized: Moves are randomized
- Start with Four Moves: Moves are randomized and all Pokemon know 4 moves at level 1

options.name: move_match_type_bias
options.description:
Sets the probability that a learned move will be forced match one of the types of a pokemon.

If a move is not forced to match type, it will roll for Normal type bias.

options.name: move_normal_type_bias
options.description:
After it has been decided that a move will not be forced to match types, sets the probability that a learned move will be forced to be the Normal type.

If a move is not forced to be Normal, it will be completely random.

options.name: tm_tutor_compatibility
options.description:
Sets the percent chance that a given TM or move tutor is compatible with a species.

Some opponents like gym leaders are allowed to use TMs. This option can affect the moves they know.

options.name: hm_compatibility
options.description:
Sets the percent chance that a given HM is compatible with a species.

Some opponents like gym leaders are allowed to use HMs. This option can affect the moves they know.

options.name: tm_tutor_moves
options.description:
Randomizes the moves taught by TMs and move tutors.

Some opponents like gym leaders are allowed to use TMs. This option can affect the moves they know.

options.name: reusable_tms_tutors
options.description: Sets TMs to not break after use (they remain sellable). Sets move tutors to infinite use.

options.name: move_blacklist
options.description:
Prevents species from learning these moves via learnsets, TMs, and move tutors.

HM moves are already banned.

options.name: min_catch_rate
options.description:
Sets the minimum catch rate a pokemon can have. Any pokemon with a catch rate below this floor will have it raised to this value.

Legendaries are often in the single digits
Fully evolved pokemon are often double digits
Pidgey is 255

options.name: guaranteed_catch
options.description: Every throw is guaranteed to catch a wild pokemon.

options.name: normalize_encounter_rates
options.description:
Make every slot on an encounter table approximately equally likely.

This does NOT mean each species is equally likely. In the vanilla game, each species may occupy more than one slot, and slots vary in probability.

Species will still occupy the same slots as vanilla, but the slots will be equally weighted. The minimum encounter rate will be 8% (higher in water).

options.name: exp_modifier
options.description:
Multiplies gained experience by a percentage.

100 is default
50 is half
200 is double
etc.

options.name: blind_trainers
options.description: Trainers will not start a battle with you unless you talk to them.

options.name: purge_spinners
options.description: Trainers will rotate in predictable patterns on a set interval instead of randomly and don't turn toward you when you run.

options.name: match_trainer_levels
options.description:
When you start a battle with a trainer, your party's levels will be automatically set to match that trainer's highest level pokemon.

The experience you receive will match your party's average actual level, and will only be awarded when you win the battle.

This is a pseudo-replacement for a level cap and makes every trainer battle a fair fight while still allowing you to level up.

- Off: The vanilla experience
- Additive: The modifier you apply to your team is a flat bonus
- Multiplicative: The modifier you apply to your team is a percent bonus

options.name: match_trainer_levels_bonus
options.description:
A level bonus (or penalty) to apply to your team when matching an opponent's levels.

When the match trainer levels option is "additive", this value is added to your team's levels during a battle.
    For example, if this value is 5 (+5 levels), you'll have a level 25 team against a level 20 team, and a level 45 team against a level 40 team.

When the match trainer levels option is "multiplicative", this is a percent bonus.
    For example, if this value is 5 (+5%), you'll have a level 21 team against a level 20 team, and a level 42 team against a level 40 team.

options.name: double_battle_chance
options.description:
The percent chance that a trainer with more than 1 pokemon will be converted into a double battle.

If these trainers would normally approach you, they will only do so if you have 2 unfainted pokemon.

They can be battled by talking to them no matter what.

options.name: better_shops
options.description: Pokemarts sell every item that can be obtained in a pokemart (except mail, which is still unique to the relevant city).

options.name: remove_roadblocks
options.description:
Removes specific NPCs that normally stand in your way until certain events are completed.

This can open up the world a bit and make your playthrough less linear, but be careful how many you remove; it may make too much of your world accessible upon receiving Surf.

options.name: extra_boulders
options.description:
Places strength boulders on Route 115 which block access to Meteor Falls from the beach.

This aims to take some power away from Surf by restricting how much it allows you to access.

options.name: extra_bumpy_slope
options.description:
Adds a bumpy slope to Route 115 which allows access to Meteor Falls if you have the Acro Bike.

This aims to take some power away from Surf by adding a new way to exit the Rustboro area.

options.name: modify_118
options.description:
Changes the layout of Route 118 so that it must be crossed with the Acro Bike instead of Surf.

This aims to take some power away from Surf by restricting how much it allows you to access.

options.name: free_fly_location
options.description: Enables flying to one random location (excluding cities reachable with no items).

options.name: free_fly_blacklist
options.description:
Disables specific locations as valid free fly locations.

Has no effect if Free Fly Location is disabled.

options.name: hm_requirements
options.description: Sets the requirements to use HMs outside of battle.

options.name: turbo_a
options.description: Holding A will advance most text automatically.

options.name: receive_item_messages
options.description:
Determines whether you receive an in-game notification when receiving an item. Items can still only be received in the overworld.

- All: Every item shows a message
- Progression: Only progression items show a message
- None: All items are added to your bag silently (badges will still show).

options.name: remote_items
options.description:
Instead of placing your own items directly into the ROM, all items are received from the server, including items you find for yourself.

This enables co-op of a single slot and recovering more items after a lost save file (if you're so unlucky).

But it changes pickup behavior slightly and requires connection to the server to receive any items.

options.name: music
options.description: Shuffles music played in any situation where it loops. Includes many FRLG tracks.

options.name: fanfares
options.description:
Shuffles fanfares for item pickups, healing at the pokecenter, etc.

When this option is enabled, pressing B will interrupt most fanfares.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

In Pokemon Emerald, whiting out sends a death and receiving a death causes you to white out.

options.name: enable_wonder_trading
options.description:
Allows participation in wonder trading with other players in your current multiworld. Speak with the center receptionist on the second floor of any pokecenter.

Wonder trading NEVER affects logic.

Certain aspects of a pokemon species are per-game, not per-pokemon. As a result, some things are not retained during a trade, including type, ability, level up learnset, and so on.

Receiving a pokemon this way does not mark it as found in your pokedex.

Trade evolutions do not evolve this way; they retain their modified methods (level ups and item use).

options.name: easter_egg
options.description:
Enter certain phrases and something special might happen.

All secret phrases are something that could be a trendy phrase in Dewford Town. They are case insensitive.

options.name: game_version
options.description: Select Red or Blue version.

options.name: trainer_name
options.description:
Your trainer name. If not set to choose_in_game, must be a name not exceeding 7 characters, and the prompt to
name your character in-game will be skipped. See the setup guide on archipelago.gg for a list of allowed characters.

options.name: rival_name
options.description:
Your rival's name. If not set to choose_in_game, must be a name not exceeding 7 characters, and the prompt to
name your rival in-game will be skipped. See the setup guide on archipelago.gg for a list of allowed characters.

options.name: elite_four_badges_condition
options.description:
Number of badges required to challenge the Elite Four once the Indigo Plateau has been reached.
Your rival will reveal the amount needed on the first Route 22 battle (after turning in Oak's Parcel).

options.name: elite_four_key_items_condition
options.description:
Percentage of available key items (not counting items you can lose) required to challenge the Elite Four. Does
not count HMs. Evolution stones and Exp. All are key items in Archipelago.

options.name: elite_four_pokedex_condition
options.description:
Percentage of logically-reachable Pokemon that must be registered as "owned" in the Pokedex in order to
challenge the Elite Four.

options.name: victory_road_condition
options.description: Number of badges required to reach the front entrance of Victory Road.

options.name: route_22_gate_condition
options.description: Number of badges required to pass through the Route 22 Gate

options.name: viridian_gym_condition
options.description: Number of badges required to enter Viridian Gym.

options.name: cerulean_cave_badges_condition
options.description: Number of badges needed to access the Cerulean Cave entrance in addition to the required Key Items.

options.name: cerulean_cave_key_items_condition
options.description:
Percentage of available key items (not counting items you can lose) required to access the Cerulean Cave
entrance in addition to the required badges. Does not count HMs.
Evolution stones and Exp. All are key items in Archipelago.

options.name: route_3_condition
options.description: Set a condition to pass through from Pewter City to Route 3.

options.name: robbed_house_officer
options.description: You can disable to remove the requirement to help Bill before you can enter the robbed house in Cerulean City.

options.name: second_fossil_check_condition
options.description:
After choosing one of the fossil location items, you can obtain the remaining item from the Cinnabar Lab
Scientist after reviving this number of fossils.

options.name: fossil_check_item_types
options.description:
The two fossil checks always contain items for your own game. Here, you can choose what types of items can
appear. Key Items means only advancement items can appear. Unique means key items or TMs may appear. No Key Items
means no advancement items may appear.

options.name: exp_all
options.description:
Choose how the Exp. All item is handled. It can be removed entirely, shuffled into the item pool, or you can
start with it.

options.name: old_man
options.description:
With Open Viridian City, the Old Man will let you through without needing to turn in Oak's Parcel.
Early Parcel will ensure Oak's Parcel is available at the beginning of your game.

options.name: badgesanity
options.description: Shuffle gym badges into the general item pool. If turned off, badges will be shuffled across the 8 gyms.

options.name: badges_needed_for_hm_moves
options.description:
Off will remove the requirement for badges to use HM moves. Extra will give the Marsh, Volcano, and Earth Badges
a random HM move to enable. Extra Plus will additionally pick two random badges to enable a second HM move.
You will only need one of the required badges to use the HM move.

options.name: key_items_only
options.description:
Shuffle only Key Items. This overrides Randomize Hidden Items, Trainersanity, and Dexsanity.
Sets all non-excluded locations in your game to Priority Locations.
May have high generation failure rates for solo games or small multiworlds, especially with Door Shuffle.

options.name: tea
options.description:
Adds a Tea item to the item pool which the Saffron guards require instead of the vending machine drinks.
Adds a location check to the Celadon Mansion 1F, where Tea is acquired in FireRed and LeafGreen.

options.name: extra_key_items
options.description:
Adds key items that are required to access the Rocket Hideout, Cinnabar Mansion, Safari Zone, and Power Plant.
Adds four item pickups to Rock Tunnel B1F.

options.name: split_card_key
options.description:
Splits the Card Key item into 10 different Keys, one for each Silph Co floor 2F through 11F.
Adds location checks to 9 NPCs in Silph Co.
With Progressive, you will always obtain the keys in order from 2F to 11F.

options.name: all_elevators_locked
options.description:
Adds requirements to the Celadon Department Store elevator and Silph Co elevators to have the Lift Key.
No logical implications normally, but may have a significant impact on some Door Shuffle options.

options.name: extra_strength_boulders
options.description:
Adds Strength Boulders blocking the Route 11 gate, and in Route 13 (can be bypassed with Surf).
This potentially increases the usefulness of Strength as well as the Bicycle.

options.name: require_item_finder
options.description: Require Item Finder to pick up hidden items.

options.name: randomize_hidden_items
options.description: Randomize hidden items. If you choose exclude, they will be randomized but will be guaranteed junk items.

options.name: prizesanity
options.description: Shuffles the TM prizes at the Celadon Prize Corner into the item pool.

options.name: trainersanity
options.description:
Add location checks to trainers, which can be obtained by talking to a trainer after defeating them. Does not
affect gym leaders and some scripted event battles. You may specify a number of trainers to have checks, and in
this case they will be randomly selected. There is no in-game indication as to which trainers have checks.

options.name: dexsanity
options.description:
Adds location checks for Pokemon flagged "owned" on your Pokedex. You may specify the exact number of Dexsanity
checks to add, and they will be distributed to Pokemon randomly.
If Accessibility is set to Full, Dexsanity checks for Pokemon that are not logically reachable will be removed,
so the number could be lower than you specified.
If Pokedex is required, the Dexsanity checks for Pokemon you acquired before acquiring the Pokedex can be found by
talking to Professor Oak or evaluating the Pokedex via Oak's PC.

options.name: randomize_pokedex
options.description: Randomize the location of the Pokedex, or start with it.

options.name: require_pokedex
options.description: Require the Pokedex to obtain items from Oak's Aides or from Dexsanity checks.

options.name: all_pokemon_seen
options.description:
Start with all Pokemon "seen" in your Pokedex. This allows you to see where Pokemon can be encountered in the
wild. Pokemon found by fishing or in the Cerulean Cave are not displayed.
The Pokedex also shows which HMs can be learned by Pokemon registered as seen.

options.name: oaks_aide_rt_2
options.description:
Number of Pokemon registered in the Pokedex required to receive the item from Oak's Aide on Route 2.
Vanilla is 10.

options.name: oaks_aide_rt_11
options.description:
Number of Pokemon registered in the Pokedex required to receive the item from Oak's Aide on Route 11.
Vanilla is 30.

options.name: oaks_aide_rt_15
options.description:
Number of Pokemon registered in the Pokedex required to receive the item from Oak's Aide on Route 15.
Vanilla is 50.

options.name: stonesanity
options.description:
Removes the four evolution stones from the Celadon Department Store and replaces four of the five Moon Stones
in the item pool with the four shop stones. If randomize_hidden_items is off, this will cause the two hidden
Moon Stone locations to be randomized anyway. These are in Pokemon Mansion 1F and Mt Moon B2F.

options.name: door_shuffle
options.description:
Simple: entrances are randomized together in groups: Pokemarts, Gyms, single exit dungeons, dual exit dungeons,
single exit misc interiors, dual exit misc interiors are all shuffled separately. Safari Zone is not shuffled.
On Simple only, the Town Map will be updated to show the new locations for each dungeon.
Interiors: Any outdoor entrance may lead to any interior, but intra-interior doors are not shuffled. Previously
named Full.
Full: Exterior to interior entrances are shuffled, and interior to interior doors are shuffled, separately.
Insanity: All doors in the game are shuffled.
Decoupled: Doors may be decoupled from each other, so that leaving through an exit may not return you to the
door you entered from.

options.name: warp_tile_shuffle
options.description:
Vanilla: The warp tiles in Silph Co and Sabrina's Gym are not changed.
Shuffle: The warp tile destinations are shuffled among themselves.
Mixed: The warp tiles are mixed into the pool of available doors for Full, Insanity, and Decoupled. Same as Shuffle
for any other door shuffle option.

options.name: randomize_rock_tunnel
options.description:
Randomize the layout of Rock Tunnel. If Full, Insanity, or Decoupled Door Shuffle is on, this will cause only the
main entrances to Rock Tunnel to be shuffled.

options.name: dark_rock_tunnel_logic
options.description: Logically require Flash to traverse the Rock Tunnel, so you are never forced to traverse it in the dark.

options.name: free_fly_location
options.description: One random Fly destination will be unlocked by default.

options.name: town_map_fly_location
options.description: One random Fly destination will be unlocked when you obtain the Town Map.

options.name: blind_trainers
options.description:
Chance each frame that you are standing on a tile in a trainer's line of sight that they will fail to initiate a
battle. If you move into and out of their line of sight without stopping, this chance will only trigger once.
Trainers which have Trainersanity location checks ignore the Blind Trainers setting.

options.name: minimum_steps_between_encounters
options.description: Minimum number of steps between wild Pokemon encounters.

options.name: level_scaling
options.description:
Off: Encounters use vanilla game levels.
By Spheres: Levels are scaled by access sphere. Areas reachable in later spheres will have higher levels.
By Spheres and Distance: Levels are scaled by access spheres as well as distance from Pallet Town, measured by
number  of internal region connections. This is a much more severe curving of levels and may lead to much less
variation in levels found in a particular map. However, it may make the higher door shuffle settings significantly
more bearable, as these options more often result in a smaller number of larger access spheres.
Auto: Scales by Spheres if Door Shuffle is off or on Simple, otherwise scales by Spheres and Distance

options.name: exp_modifier
options.description: Modifier for EXP gained. When specifying a number, exp is multiplied by this amount and divided by 16.

options.name: randomize_wild_pokemon
options.description:
Randomize all wild Pokemon and game corner prize Pokemon. match_types will select a Pokemon with at least one
type matching the original type of the original Pokemon. match_base_stats will prefer Pokemon with closer base stat
totals. match_types_and_base_stats will match types and will weight towards similar base stats, but there may not be
many to choose from.

options.name: area_1_to_1_mapping
options.description:
When randomizing wild Pokemon, for each zone, all instances of a particular Pokemon will be replaced with the
same Pokemon, resulting in fewer Pokemon in each area.

options.name: randomize_starter_pokemon
options.description: Randomize the starter Pokemon choices.

options.name: randomize_static_pokemon
options.description: Randomize one-time gift and encountered Pokemon. These will always be first evolution stage Pokemon.

options.name: randomize_legendary_pokemon
options.description:
Randomize Legendaries. Mew has been added as an encounter at the Vermilion dock truck.
Shuffle will shuffle the legendaries with each other. Static will shuffle them into other static Pokemon locations.
'Any' will allow legendaries to appear anywhere based on wild and static randomization options, and their locations
will be randomized according to static Pokemon randomization options.

options.name: catch_em_all
options.description:
Guarantee all first evolution stage Pokemon are available, or all Pokemon of all stages.
Currently only has an effect if wild Pokemon are randomized.

options.name: randomize_pokemon_stats
options.description:
Randomize base stats for each Pokemon. Shuffle will shuffle the 5 base stat values amongst each other. Randomize
will completely randomize each stat, but will still add up to the same base stat total.

options.name: randomize_pokemon_catch_rates
options.description: Randomize the catch rate for each Pokemon.

options.name: minimum_catch_rate
options.description:
Minimum catch rate for each Pokemon. If randomize_catch_rates is on, this will be the minimum value that can be
chosen. Otherwise, it will raise any Pokemon's catch rate up to this value if its normal catch rate is lower.

options.name: randomize_trainer_parties
options.description: Randomize enemy Pokemon encountered in trainer battles.

options.name: trainer_legendaries
options.description: Allow legendary Pokemon in randomized trainer parties.

options.name: move_balancing
options.description:
All one-hit-KO moves and fixed-damage moves become normal damaging moves.
Blizzard, and moves that cause sleep have their accuracy reduced.

options.name: fix_combat_bugs
options.description:
Fixes a variety of combat-related bugs. Note that this fixes the Focus Energy bug. The Focus Energy bug causes
critical strike chances to be doubled when Focus Energy has not been used and halved when it is used.
Fixing this bug means critical strike chances outside the use of Focus Energy are quartered from the vanilla rate.

options.name: randomize_pokemon_movesets
options.description: Randomize the moves learned by Pokemon. prefer_types will prefer moves that match the type of the Pokemon.

options.name: confine_transform_to_ditto
options.description:
Regardless of moveset randomization, will keep Ditto's first move as Transform no others will learn it.
If an enemy Pokemon uses transform before you catch it, it will permanently change to Ditto after capture.

options.name: start_with_four_moves
