options.description: If movesets are randomized, this will give all Pokemon 4 starting moves.

options.name: same_type_attack_bonus
options.description:
Here you can disable Same Type Attack Bonus, so that a move matching a Pokemon's type has no benefit.
If disabled, all moves will gain 25% extra damage, instead of same type moves gaining 50% extra damage.

options.name: randomize_tm_moves
options.description:
Randomize the moves taught by TMs.
All TM items will be flagged as 'filler' items regardless of how good the move they teach are.

options.name: tm_same_type_compatibility
options.description: Chance of each TM being usable on each Pokemon whose type matches the move.

options.name: tm_normal_type_compatibility
options.description: Chance of each TM being usable on each Pokemon if the move is Normal type and the Pokemon is not.

options.name: tm_other_type_compatibility
options.description: Chance of each TM being usable on each Pokemon if the move a type other than Normal or one of the Pokemon's types.

options.name: hm_same_type_compatibility
options.description:
Chance of each HM being usable on each Pokemon whose type matches the move.
At least one Pokemon will always be able to learn the moves needed to meet your accessibility requirements.

options.name: hm_normal_type_compatibility
options.description:
Chance of each HM being usable on each Pokemon if the move is Normal type and the Pokemon is not.
At least one Pokemon will always be able to learn the moves needed to meet your accessibility requirements.

options.name: hm_other_type_compatibility
options.description:
Chance of each HM being usable on each Pokemon if the move a type other than Normal or one of the Pokemon's types.
At least one Pokemon will always be able to learn the moves needed to meet your accessibility requirements.

options.name: inherit_tm_hm_compatibility
options.description:
If on, evolved Pokemon will inherit their pre-evolved form's TM and HM compatibilities.
They will then roll the above set chances again at a 50% lower rate for all TMs and HMs their predecessor could not
learn, unless the evolved form has additional or different types, then moves of those new types will be rolled
at the full set chance.

options.name: randomize_move_types
options.description: Randomize the types of each move.

options.name: randomize_pokemon_types
options.description:
Randomize the types of each Pokemon. Follow Evolutions will ensure Pokemon's types remain the same when evolving
(except possibly gaining a type).

options.name: secondary_type_chance
options.description:
If randomize_pokemon_types is on, this is the chance each Pokemon will have a secondary type. If follow_evolutions
is selected, it is the chance a second type will be added at each evolution stage. vanilla will give secondary types
to Pokemon that normally have a secondary type.

options.name: randomize_type_chart
options.description:
Randomize the type chart. If 'randomize' is chosen, the matchup weight options will determine the weights.
If the numbers chosen across the 4 settings add up to exactly 225, they will be the exact numbers of those matchups.
Otherwise, the normal super effective, and not very effective matchup settings will be used as weights.
The immunities option will always be the exact amount of immunity matchups.
If 'chaos' is chosen, the matchup settings will be ignored and every type matchup will be given a random damage
modifier anywhere between 0 to 200% damage, in 10% increments.

options.name: normal_matchups
options.description:
If 'randomize' is chosen for Randomize Type Chart, this will be the weight for neutral matchups.
No effect if 'chaos' is chosen

options.name: super_effective_matchups
options.description:
If 'randomize' is chosen for Randomize Type Chart, this will be the weight for super effective matchups.
No effect if 'chaos' is chosen

options.name: not_very_effective_matchups
options.description:
If 'randomize' is chosen for Randomize Type Chart, this will be the weight for not very effective matchups.
No effect if 'chaos' is chosen

options.name: immunity_matchups
options.description:
If 'randomize' is chosen for Randomize Type Chart, this will be the exact number of immunities.
No effect if 'chaos' is chosen

options.name: type_chart_seed
options.description:
You can enter a number to use as a seed for the type chart. If you enter anything besides a number or "random",
it will be used as a type chart group name, and everyone using the same group name will get the same type chart,
made using the type chart options of one random player within the group. If a group name is used, the type matchup
information will not be made available for trackers.

options.name: safari_zone_normal_battles
options.description: Change the Safari Zone to have standard wild Pokemon battles.

options.name: normalize_encounter_chances
options.description:
Each wild encounter table has 10 slots for Pokemon. Normally the chance for each being chosen ranges from
19.9% to 1.2%. Turn this on to normalize them all to 10% each.

options.name: reusable_tms
options.description: Makes TMs reusable, so they will not be consumed upon use.

options.name: better_shops
options.description:
Change every town's Pokemart to contain all normal Pokemart items. Additionally, you can add the Master Ball
to these shops.

options.name: master_ball_price
options.description:
Price for Master Balls. Can only be bought if Better Shops is set to Add Master Ball, but this will affect the
sell price regardless. Vanilla is 0

options.name: starting_money
options.description: The amount of money you start with.

options.name: lose_money_on_blackout
options.description: Lose half your money when blacking out, as in vanilla.

options.name: poke_doll_skip
options.description: Patch out the Pokemon Tower Poke Doll skip or have this skip considered in logic.

options.name: bicycle_gate_skips
options.description: Patch out the Route 16/18 Bicycle Gate skips or have these skips considered in logic.

options.name: trap_percentage
options.description:
Chance for each filler item to be replaced with trap items. Keep in mind that trainersanity vastly increases the
number of filler items. The trap weight options will determine which traps can be chosen from and at what likelihood.

options.name: poison_trap_weight
options.description: Weights for Poison Traps. These apply the Poison status to all your party members.

options.name: fire_trap_weight
options.description: Weights for Fire Traps. These apply the Burn status to all your party members.

options.name: paralyze_trap_weight
options.description: Weights for Paralyze Traps. These apply the Paralyze status to all your party members.

options.name: sleep_trap_weight
options.description: Weights for Sleep Traps. These apply the Sleep status to all your party members, for randomly between 1 and 7 turns.

options.name: ice_trap_weight
options.description: Weights for Ice Traps. These apply the Ice status to all your party members. Don't forget to buy Ice Heals!

options.name: randomize_pokemon_palettes
options.description:
Modify Super Gameboy palettes of Pokemon. Primary Type will set Pokemons' palettes based on their primary type,
Follow Evolutions will randomize palettes but they will remain the same through evolutions (except Eeveelutions),
Completely Random will randomize all Pokemons' palettes individually

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: minimum_resource_pack_amount
options.description: The minimum amount of resources available in a resource pack

options.name: maximum_resource_pack_amount
options.description: The maximum amount of resources available in a resource pack

options.name: duplicate_items
options.description:
Adds duplicates of items to the item pool (if configured in Filler items). These will be selected alongside
Resource Packs (if configured). Note that there are not many progression items, and selecting Progression may
produce many of the same duplicate item.

options.name: filler_item_types
options.description: Determines whether to use Resource Packs, Duplicate Items (as configured), or both.

options.name: island_frequency_locations
options.description:
Sets where frequencies for story islands are located.
Vanilla will keep frequencies in their vanilla, non-randomized locations.
Random On Island will randomize each frequency within its vanilla island, but will preserve island order.
Random Island Order will change the order you visit islands, but will preserve the vanilla location of each frequency unlock.
Random On Island Random Order will randomize the location containing the frequency on each island and randomize the order.
Progressive will randomize the frequencies to anywhere, but will always unlock the frequencies in vanilla order as the frequency items are received.
Anywhere will randomize the frequencies to anywhere, and frequencies will be received in any order.

options.name: island_generation_distance
options.description: Sets how far away islands spawn from you when you input their coordinates into the Receiver.

options.name: expensive_research
options.description:
If No is selected, researching items and unlocking items in the Crafting Table works the same as vanilla Raft.
If Yes is selected, each unlock in the Crafting Table will require its own set of researched items in order to unlock it.

options.name: progressive_items
options.description: Makes some items, like the Bow and Arrow, progressive rather than raw unlocks.

options.name: big_island_early_crafting
options.description:
Allows recipes that require items from big islands (eg leather) to lock earlygame items like the Receiver, Bolt,
or Smelter. Big islands are available from the start of the game, however it can take a long time to find them.

options.name: paddleboard_mode
options.description: Sets later story islands to be in logic without an Engine or Steering Wheel. May require lots of paddling.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Classic Mode: Every Item pickup increases fills a progress bar which gives location checks.

Explore Mode: Each environment will have location checks within each environment.
environments will be locked in the item pool until received.

options.name: victory
options.description:
Mithrix: Defeat Mithrix in Commencement
Voidling: Defeat the Voidling in The Planetarium (SOTV DLC required! Will select any if not enabled.)
Limbo: Defeat the Scavenger in Hidden Realm: A Moment, Whole
Falseson: Defeat False son and gift an item to the altar in Prime Meridian (SOTS DLC required! Will select any if not enabled.)
Any: Any victory in the game will count. See Final Stage Death for additional ways.

options.name: total_revivals
options.description: Total Percentage of `Dio's Best Friend` item put in the item pool.

options.name: start_with_revive
options.description: Start the game with a `Dio's Best Friend` item.

options.name: final_stage_death
options.description:
The following will count as a win if set to "true", and victory is set to "any":
Dying in Commencement.
Dying in The Planetarium.
Obliterating yourself
If not use the following to tell if final stage death will count:
Victory: mithrix - only dying in Commencement will count.
Victory: voidling - only dying in The Planetarium will count.
Victory: limbo - Obliterating yourself will count.
Victory: falseson - only dying in Prime Meridian will count.

options.name: dlc_sotv
options.description:
Enable if you are using Survivors of the Void DLC.
Affects environment availability for Explore Mode.
Adds Void Items into the item pool

options.name: dlc_sots
options.description:
Enable if you are using Seekers of the Storm DLC.
Affects environment availability for Explore Mode.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: item_pickup_step
options.description:
Number of items to pick up before an AP Check is completed.
Setting to 1 means every other pickup.
Setting to 2 means every third pickup. So on...

options.name: shrine_use_step
options.description:
Explore Mode:
Number of shrines to use up before an AP Check is completed.
Setting to 1 means every other pickup.
Setting to 2 means every third pickup. So on...

options.name: enable_trap
options.description: Allows Trap items in the item pool.

options.name: enable_lunar
options.description: Allows Lunar items in the item pool.

options.name: chests_per_stage
options.description: Explore Mode: The number of chest locations per environment.

options.name: shrines_per_stage
options.description: Explore Mode: The number of shrine locations per environment.

options.name: scavengers_per_stage
options.description: Explore Mode: The number of scavenger locations per environment.

options.name: scanner_per_stage
options.description: Explore Mode: The number of scanners locations per environment.

options.name: altars_per_stage
options.description: Explore Mode: The number of altars locations per environment.

options.name: require_stages
options.description: Add Stage items to the pool to block access to the next set of environments.

options.name: progressive_stages
options.description:
This will convert Stage items to be a progressive item. For example instead of "Stage 2" it would be
"Progressive Stage"

options.name: stage_variants
options.description:
Enable if you want to include stage variants in the environment pool.
Stages included are:
- Distant Roost (2)
- Titanic Plains (2)
SOTS DLC Enabled:
- Vicious Falls
- Shattered Abodes
- Golden Dieback

options.name: show_seer_portals
options.description: Shows Seer Portals at the teleporter to allow choosing the next environment.

options.name: total_locations
options.description: Classic Mode: Number of location checks which are added to the Risk of Rain playthrough.

options.name: item_weights
options.description:
Set Use Item Weight Presets to yes if you want to use one of these presets.
Preset choices for determining the weights of the item pool.
- New is a test for a potential adjustment to the default weights.
- Uncommon puts a large number of uncommon items in the pool.
- Legendary puts a large number of legendary items in the pool.
- Chaos generates the pool completely at random with rarer items having a slight cap to prevent this option being
too easy.
- No Scraps removes all scrap items from the item pool.
- Even generates the item pool with every item having an even weight.
- Scraps Only will be only scrap items in the item pool.
- Lunartic makes everything a lunar item.
- Void makes everything a void item.

options.name: item_pool_presets
options.description: Will use the item weight presets when set to true, otherwise will use the custom set item pool weights.

options.name: white_scrap
options.description:
Weight of white scraps in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: green_scrap
options.description:
Weight of Green Scraps in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: yellow_scrap
options.description:
Weight of yellow scraps in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: red_scrap
options.description:
Weight of Red Scraps in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: common_item
options.description:
Weight of common items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: uncommon_item
options.description:
Weight of uncommon items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: legendary_item
options.description:
Weight of legendary items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: boss_item
options.description:
Weight of boss items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: lunar_item
options.description:
Weight of lunar items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: void_item
options.description:
Weight of void items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

(Ignored if Enable DLC - SOTV is 'No')

options.name: equipment
options.description:
Weight of equipment items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: money
options.description:
Weight of money items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: lunar_coin
options.description:
Weight of lunar coin items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: experience
options.description:
Weight of 1000 exp items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: mountain_trap
options.description:
Weight of mountain trap items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: time_warp_trap
options.description:
Weight of time warp trap items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: combat_trap
options.description:
Weight of combat trap items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: teleport_trap
options.description:
Weight of teleport trap items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.name: gate_boss_plando
options.description:
Possible Locations:
"Gate 1 Boss"
"Gate 2 Boss"
"Gate 3 Boss"
"Gate 4 Boss"
"Gate 5 Boss"

Possible Bosses:
"Sonic vs Shadow 1"
"Sonic vs Shadow 2"
"Tails vs Eggman 1"
"Tails vs Eggman 2"
"Knuckles vs Rouge 1"
"BIG FOOT"
"HOT SHOT"
"FLYING DOG"
"Egg Golem (Sonic)"
"Egg Golem (Eggman)"
"King Boom Boo"

options.name: ring_link
options.description: Whether your in-level ring gain/loss is linked to other players

options.name: trap_link
options.description:
Whether your received traps are linked to other players

You will also receive any linked traps from other players with Trap Link enabled,
if you have a weight above "none" set for that trap

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: goal
options.description:
Determines the goal of the seed

Biolizard: Finish Cannon's Core and defeat the Biolizard and Finalhazard

Chaos Emerald Hunt: Find the Seven Chaos Emeralds and reach Green Hill Zone

Finalhazard Chaos Emerald Hunt: Find the Seven Chaos Emeralds and reach Green Hill Zone, then defeat Finalhazard

Grand Prix: Win every race in Kart Race Mode (all standard levels are disabled)

Boss Rush: Beat all of the bosses in the Boss Rush, ending with Finalhazard

Cannon's Core Boss Rush: Beat Cannon's Core, then beat all of the bosses in the Boss Rush, ending with Finalhazard

Boss Rush Chaos Emerald Hunt: Find the Seven Chaos Emeralds, then beat all of the bosses in the Boss Rush, ending with Finalhazard

Chaos Chao: Raise a Chaos Chao to win

Minigame Madness: Win a certain amount of each Minigame Trap, then defeat Finalhazard

options.name: boss_rush_shuffle
options.description:
Determines how bosses in Boss Rush Mode are shuffled

Vanilla: Bosses appear in the Vanilla ordering

Shuffled: The same bosses appear, but in a random order

Chaos: Each boss is randomly chosen separately (one will always be King Boom Boo)

Singularity: One boss is chosen and placed in every slot (one will always be replaced with King Boom Boo)

options.name: minigame_madness_requirement
options.description:
Determines how many of each Minigame Trap must be won (for Minigame Madness goal)

options.name: final_elevator_phase
options.description:
Put the milestones accessible BEFORE this Space Elevator Phase in logic.
Milestones after the selected Phase are empty and contain nothing.
If your goal selection contains *Space Elevator Phase* then submitting this Phase's elevator package completes that goal.
If the goal is not enabled, this setting simply limits the HUB's content.

Estimated in-game completion times:

- **Phase 1 (Tiers 1-2)**: ~3 Hours
- **Phase 2 (Tiers 1-4)**: ~8 Hours
- **Phase 3 (Tiers 1-6)**: ~50 Hours
- **Phase 4 (Tiers 1-8)**: ~100 Hours
- **Phase 5 (Tiers 1-9)**: ~150 Hours

options.name: goal_selection
options.description:
What will be your goal(s)?
Configure them further with other options.

Possible values are:
- **Space Elevator Phase**
- **AWESOME Sink Points (total)**
- **AWESOME Sink Points (per minute)**
- **Exploration Collectables**

options.name: goal_requirement
options.description: Of the goals selected in *Select your Goals*, how many must be reached to complete your slot?

options.name: goal_awesome_sink_points_total
options.description:
Does nothing if *AWESOME Sink Points (total)* goal is not enabled.

Sink an amount of items totalling this amount of points to finish.
This setting is a *point count*, not a *coupon* count!

In the base game, it takes 347 coupons to unlock every non-repeatable purchase, or 1895 coupons to purchase every non-producible item.

Use the **TFIT - Ficsit Information Tool** mod or the Satisfactory wiki to find out how many points items are worth.

If you have *Free Samples* enabled, consider setting this higher so that you can't reach the goal just by sinking your Free Samples.

options.name: goal_awesome_sink_points_per_minute
options.description:
Does nothing if *AWESOME Sink Points (per minute)* goal is not enabled.

Sink items to maintain a sink points per minute of the chosen amount for 10 minutes to finish.
This setting is in *points per minute* on the orange track, so DNA Capsules don't count.
This option's presets are example production thresholds - you don't have to sink exactly those specific items.

Use the **TFIT - Ficsit Information Tool** mod or the Satisfactory wiki to find out how many points items are worth.

options.name: goal_exploration_collectables_amount
options.description:
Does nothing if *Exploration Collectables* goal is not enabled.

Collect this amount of Mercer Spheres, Somersloops, Hard Drives, Paleberries, Beryl Nuts, and Bacon Agarics each to finish.

- The amount of **Mercer Spheres** is **2x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Somersloops** is **the** selected amount
- The amount of **Hard Drives** is **1/5th** the selected amount
- The amount of **Paleberries** is **10x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Beryl Nuts** is **20x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Bacon Agarics** is **the** selected amount

options.name: starting_inventory_preset
options.description:
What resources (and buildings) the player should start with in their inventory.
If you want more control, visit the Weighted Options page or edit the YAML directly.

- **Barebones**: Nothing but the default xeno zapper and buildings.
- **Skip Tutorial Inspired**: Inspired by the items you would have if you skipped the base game's tutorial.
- **Archipelago**: The starting items we think will lead to a fun experience.
- **Foundations**: 'Archipelago' option, but also guaranteeing that you have foundations unlocked at the start.
- **Foundation Lover**: You really like foundations.
- **Explorer**: 'Foundations' option plus one set of early exploration equipment (Parachute, Blade Runners, Object Scanner, Boom Box).

options.name: goal
options.description:
Sets the goal of your world.

- **Vanilla:** Complete level 26.
- **MAM:** Complete a specified level after level 26. Every level before that will be a location. It's recommended
  to build a Make-Anything-Machine (MAM).
- **Even fasterer:** Upgrade everything to a specified tier after tier 8. Every upgrade before that will be a
  location.
- **Efficiency III:** Deliver 256 blueprint shapes per second to the hub.

options.name: goal_amount
options.description:
Specify, what level or tier (when either MAM or Even Fasterer is chosen as goal) is required to reach the goal.

If MAM is set as the goal, this has to be set to 27 or more. Else it will raise an error.

options.name: required_shapes_multiplier
options.description:
Multiplies the amount of required shapes for levels and upgrades by value/10.

For level 1, the amount of shapes ranges from 3 to 300.

For level 26, it ranges from 5k to 500k.

options.name: allow_floating_layers
options.description:
Toggle whether shape requirements are allowed to have floating layers (like the logo or the rocket shape).

However, be aware that floating shapes make MAMs much more complex.

options.name: randomize_level_requirements
options.description: Randomize the required shapes to complete levels.

options.name: randomize_upgrade_requirements
options.description: Randomize the required shapes to buy upgrades.

options.name: randomize_level_logic
options.description:
If level requirements are randomized, this sets how those random shapes are generated and how logic works for
levels. The shuffled variants shuffle the order of progression buildings obtained in the multiworld. The standard
order is: **cutter -> rotator -> painter -> color mixer -> stacker**

- **Vanilla:** Level 1 requires nothing, 2-4 require the first building, 5-6 require also the second, 7-8 the
  third, 9-10 the fourth, and 11 and onwards the fifth and thereby all buildings.
- **Stretched:** After every floor(maxlevel/6) levels, another building is required.
- **Quick:** Every Level, except level 1, requires another building, with level 6 and onwards requiring all
  buildings.
- **Random steps:** After a random amount of levels, another building is required, with level 1 always requiring
  none. This can potentially generate like any other option.
- **Hardcore:** All levels (except level 1) have completely random shape requirements and thus require all
  buildings. Expect early BKs.
- **Dopamine (overflow):** All levels (except level 1 and the goal) require 2 random buildings (or none in case of
  overflow).

options.name: randomize_upgrade_logic
options.description:
If upgrade requirements are randomized, this sets how those random shapes are generated
and how logic works for upgrades.

- **Vanilla-like:** Tier II requires up to two random buildings, III requires up to three random buildings,
  and IV and onwards require all processing buildings.
- **Linear:** Tier II requires nothing, III-VI require another random building each,
  and VII and onwards require all buildings.
- **Category:** Belt and miner upgrades require no building up to tier V, but onwards all buildings, processors
  upgrades require the cutter (all tiers), rotator (tier III and onwards), and stacker (tier V and onwards), and
  painting upgrades require the cutter, rotator, stacker, painter (all tiers) and color mixer (tiers V and onwards).
  Tier VII and onwards will always require all buildings.
- **Category random:** Each upgrades category (up to tier VI) requires a random amount of buildings (in order),
  with one category always requiring no buildings. Tier VII and onwards will always require all buildings.
- **Hardcore:** All tiers (except each tier II) have completely random shape requirements and thus require all
  buildings. Expect early BKs.

options.name: throughput_levels_ratio
options.description:
If level requirements are randomized, this sets the ratio of how many levels (approximately) will require either
a total amount or per second amount (throughput) of shapes delivered.

0 means only total, 100 means only throughput, and vanilla (-1) means only levels 14, 27 and beyond have throughput.

options.name: complexity_growth_gradient
options.description:
If level requirements are randomized, this determines how fast complexity will grow each level. In other words:
The higher you set this value, the more difficult lategame shapes will be.

Allowed values are floating numbers ranging from 0.0 to 10.0.

options.name: same_late_upgrade_requirements
options.description:
If upgrade requirements are randomized, should the last 3 shapes for each category be the same,
as in vanilla?

options.name: early_balancer_tunnel_and_trash
options.description:
Makes the balancer, tunnel, and trash appear in earlier spheres.

- **None:** Complete randomization.
- **5 buildings:** Should be accessible before getting all 5 main buildings.
- **3 buildings:** Should be accessible before getting the first 3 main buildings for levels and upgrades.
- **Sphere 1:** Always accessible from start. **Beware of generation failures.**

options.name: lock_belt_and_extractor
options.description:
Locks Belts and Extractors and adds them to the item pool.

**If you set this to true, achievements must also be included.**

options.name: include_achievements
options.description: Include up to 45 achievements (depending on other options) as additional locations.

options.name: exclude_softlock_achievements
options.description: Exclude 6 achievements, that can become unreachable in a save file, if not achieved until a certain level.

options.name: exclude_long_playtime_achievements
options.description: Exclude 2 achievements, that require actively playing for a really long time.

options.name: exclude_progression_unreasonable
options.description: Exclude progression and useful items from being placed into softlock and long playtime achievements.

options.name: shapesanity_amount
options.description: Amount of single-layer shapes that will be included as locations.

options.name: traps_percentage
options.description: The probability of any filler item (in percent) being replaced by a trap.

options.name: include_whacky_upgrades
options.description:
Includes some very unusual upgrade items in generation (and logic), that greatly increase or decrease building
speeds. If the goal is set to Efficiency III or throughput levels ratio is not 0, decreasing upgrades (aka traps)
will always be disabled.

options.name: split_inventory_draining_trap
options.description:
If set to true, the inventory draining trap will be split into level, upgrade, and blueprint draining traps
instead of executing as one of those 3 randomly.

options.name: toolbar_shuffling
options.description:
If set to true, the toolbars (main and wires layer) will be shuffled (including bottom and top row).
However, keybindings will still select the same building to place.

options.name: ixupi_captures_needed
options.description: Number of Ixupi Captures needed for goal condition.

options.name: lobby_access
options.description:
Chooses how keys needed to reach the lobby are placed.
- Normal: Keys are placed anywhere
- Early: Keys are placed early 
- Local: Keys are placed locally and early

options.name: puzzle_hints_required
options.description:
If turned on puzzle hints/solutions will be available before the corresponding puzzle is required.

For example: The Red Door puzzle will be logically required only after obtaining access to Beth's Address Book
which gives you the solution.

Turning this off allows for greater randomization.

options.name: include_information_plaques
options.description:
Adds Information Plaques as checks.
(40 Locations)

options.name: front_door_usable
options.description: Adds a key to unlock the front door of the museum.

options.name: elevators_stay_solved
options.description:
Adds elevators as checks and will remain open upon solving them.
(3 Locations)

options.name: early_beth
options.description:
Beth's body is open at the start of the game.
This allows any pot piece to be placed in the slide and early checks on the second half of the final riddle.

options.name: early_lightning
options.description:
Allows lightning to be captured at any point in the game. You will still need to capture all ten Ixupi for victory.
(1 Location)

options.name: location_pot_pieces
options.description:
Chooses where pot pieces will be located within the multiworld.
- Own World: Pot pieces will be located within your own world
- Different World: Pot pieces will be located in another world
- Any World: Pot pieces will be located in any world

options.name: full_pots
options.description:
Chooses if pots will be in pieces or already completed
- Pieces: Only pot pieces will be added to the item pool
- Complete: Only completed pots will be added to the item pool
- Mixed: Each pot will be randomly chosen to be pieces or already completed.

options.name: ixupi_captures_priority
options.description: Ixupi captures are set to priority locations. This forces a progression item into these locations if possible.

options.name: puzzle_collect_behavior
options.description:
Defines what happens to puzzles on collect.
- Solve None: No puzzles will be solved when collected.
- Prevent Out Of Logic Access: All puzzles, except Red Door and Skull Door, will be solved when collected.
This prevents out of logic access to Gods Room and Slide.
- Solve All: All puzzles will be solved when collected. (original behavior)

options.name: goal
options.description:
Choose the end goal.
Nap: Complete the climb to the top of Hawk Peak and take a nap
Photo: Get your picture taken at the top of Hawk Peak
Races: Complete all three races with Avery
Help Everyone: Travel around Hawk Peak and help every character with their troubles
Fishmonger: Catch one of every fish from around Hawk Peak

options.name: filler_coin_amount
options.description: The number of coins that will be in each filler coin item.

options.name: random_walkie_talkie
options.description:
When enabled, the Walkie Talkie item will be placed into the item pool. Otherwise, it will be placed in its vanilla location.
This item usually allows the player to locate Avery around the map or restart a race.

options.name: golden_feather_progression
options.description:
Determines which locations are considered in logic based on the required amount of golden feathers to reach them.
Easy: Locations will be considered inaccessible until the player has enough golden feathers to easily reach them. A minimum of 10 golden feathers is recommended for this setting.
Normal: Locations will be considered inaccessible until the player has the minimum possible number of golden feathers to reach them. A minimum of 7 golden feathers is recommended for this setting.
Hard: Removes the requirement of golden feathers for progression entirely and glitches may need to be used to progress

options.name: easier_races
options.description: When enabled, the Running Shoes will be added as a logical requirement for beating any of the races.

options.name: golden_feathers
options.description:
Number of Golden Feathers in the item pool.
(Note that for the Photo and Help Everyone goals, a minimum of 12 Golden Feathers is enforced)

options.name: silver_feathers
options.description: Number of Silver Feathers in the item pool.

options.name: buckets
options.description: Number of Buckets in the item pool.

options.name: sticks
options.description: Number of Sticks in the item pool.

options.name: toy_shovels
options.description: Number of Toy Shovels in the item pool.

options.name: coins_in_shops
options.description: When enabled, the randomizer can place coins into locations that are purchased, such as shops.

options.name: cost_multiplier
options.description: The percentage that all item shop costs will be of the vanilla values.

options.name: shop_check_logic
options.description: Determines which items will be added as logical requirements to making certain purchases in shops.

options.name: min_shop_check_logic
options.description:
Determines the minimum cost of a shop item that will have the shop check logic applied to it.
If the cost of a shop item is less than this value, no items will be required to access it.
This is based on the vanilla prices of the shop item. The set cost multiplier will not affect this value.

options.name: start_inventory_removes_from_pool
options.description: Remove items in starting inventory from pool.

options.name: remote_items
options.description:
Items from your own world are sent via the Archipelago server. This allows co-op play of a world and means that
you will not lose items on death or save file loss.

options.name: death_link
options.description:
When DeathLink is enabled and someone else with DeathLink dies, you will die. 
If "Enable Survive" is selected, reserve tanks can save you.

options.name: preset
options.description:
Determines the general difficulty of the item placements by adjusting the list of tricks that logic allows.
- Newbie: New to randomizers, but completed Super Metroid 100% and knows basic techniques (Wall Jump, Shinespark, Mid-air Morph)
- Casual: Occasional rando player. No hell runs or suitless Maridia, some easy to learn tricks in logic.
- Regular: Plays rando regularly. Knows many tricks that open up the game.
- Veteran: Experienced rando player. Harder everything, some tougher tricks in logic.
- Expert: Knows almost all tricks: full suitless Maridia, Lower Norfair hell runs, etc.
- Master: Everything on hardest, all tricks known.
In-depth details on each preset can be found on the VARIA website: https://varia.run/presets
You may also specify "varia_custom" to use varia_custom_preset option, or specify "custom" to use custom_preset option.

options.name: max_difficulty
options.description:
Maximum difficulty of tricks that are allowed from the seed's Preset.
Depending on the perceived difficulties of the techniques, bosses, hell runs etc. from the preset, it will
prevent the Randomizer from placing an item in a location too difficult to reach with the current items.

options.name: start_location
options.description: Choose where you want to start the game.

options.name: varia_custom_preset
options.description: use an entry from the preset list on https://varia.run/presets

options.name: objective
options.description:
If ""Custom objectives"" is disabled, choose which objectives are required to sink the Golden Four statue and to open access to Tourian.
You can choose from 0 to 5 objectives. Up to the first 5 objectives from the list will be selected.
Note: If you leave the list empty no objective is required to access Tourian, ie. it's open.
Note: See the Tourian parameter to enable fast Tourian or trigger the escape when all objectives are completed.
Note: Current percentage of collected items is displayed in the inventory pause menu.
Note: In AP, Items% and areas objectives are counted toward location checks, not items collected or received, except for "collect all upgrades"

Format as a comma-separated list of objective names: ["kill three G4", "collect 75% items"]. The default is ["kill all G4"].
A full list of supported objectives can be found at:
https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/blob/main/worlds/sm/variaRandomizer/utils/objectives.py

options.name: custom_objective
options.description:
Use randomized custom objectives. You can choose which objectives are available for the randomizer to choose from. If enabled, the randomizer 
will choose "Custom objective count" objectives from "Custom objective list". Otherwise, only objective is used. Default is disabled.

options.name: custom_objective_count
options.description:
By default you need to complete 4 objectives from the list to access Tourian. You can choose between 1 and 5. This setting is ignored if
""Custom objectives"" is set to false.

options.name: custom_objective_list
options.description:
If ""Custom objectives"" is enabled, "Custom Objective count" will be used to pick an amount of objective from the list.
This setting is ignored if ""Custom objectives"" is set to false.
Note: If you leave the list empty no objective is required to access Tourian, ie. it's open.
Note: See the Tourian parameter to enable fast Tourian or trigger the escape when all objectives are completed.
Note: Current percentage of collected items is displayed in the inventory pause menu.
Note: Collect 100% items is excluded by default as it requires you to complete all the objectives.
Note: In AP, Items% and areas objectives are counted toward location checks, not items collected or received, except for "collect all upgrades"

Format as a comma-separated list of objective names: ["kill three G4", "collect 75% items"] or ["random"] to specify the whole list except
"collect 100% items" and "nothing". The default is ["random"]. A full list of supported objectives can be found at:
https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/blob/main/worlds/sm/variaRandomizer/utils/objectives.py

options.name: tourian
options.description:
Choose endgame Tourian behaviour:
- Vanilla: regular vanilla Tourian
- Fast: speed up Tourian to skip Metroids, Zebetites, and all cutscenes (including Mother Brain 3 fight). Golden Four statues are replaced by an invincible Gadora until all objectives are completed.
- Disabled: skip Tourian entirely; the escape sequence is triggered as soon as all objectives are completed.

options.name: escape_rando
options.description:
When leaving Tourian, get teleported to the exit of a random Map station (between Brinstar/Maridia/Norfair/Wrecked Ship).
You then have to find your way to the ship in the remaining time. Allotted time depends on area layout, but not on skill settings and is pretty generous.

During the escape sequence:
- All doors are opened
- Maridia tube is opened
- The Hyper Beam can destroy Bomb, Power Bomb and Super Missile blocks and open blue/green gates from both sides
- All mini bosses are defeated
- All minor enemies are removed to allow you to move faster and remove lag

During regular game only Crateria Map station door can be opened and activating the station will act as if all map stations were activated at once.

Animals Challenges:
You can use the extra available time to:
- find the animals that are hidden behind a (now blue) map station door
- go to the vanilla animals door to cycle through the 4 available escapes, and complete as many escapes as you can

Pick your challenge, or try to do both, but watch your timer!

options.name: remove_escape_enemies
options.description: Remove enemies during escape sequence, disable it to blast through enemies with your Hyper Beam and cause lag.

options.name: animals
options.description:
Replace saving the animals in the escape sequence by a random surprise.
Note: This setting is not available when Escape Randomization is enabled, as it is replaced by Animals Challenges
(see Escape Randomization help for more information).

options.name: area_randomization
options.description:
Randomize areas together using bidirectional access portals.
- Off: No change. All rooms are connected the same as in the original game.
- Full: All doors connecting areas will be randomized. "Areas" are roughly determined, but generally are regions
with different tilesets or music. For example, red Brinstar and green/pink Brinstar are different areas, Crocomire
and upper Norfair are different areas, etc.
- Light: Keep the same number of transitions between areas as in vanilla. So Crocomire area will always be connected
to upper Norfair, there'll always be two transitions between Crateria/blue Brinstar and green/pink Brinstar, etc.

options.name: area_layout
options.description: Some layout tweaks to make your life easier in areas randomizer.

options.name: doors_colors_rando
options.description:
Randomize the color of Red/Green/Yellow doors. Add four new types of doors which require Ice/Wave/Spazer/Plasma
Beams to open them.

options.name: allow_grey_doors
options.description:
When randomizing the color of Red/Green/Yellow doors, some doors can be randomized to Grey. Grey doors will never
open; you will have to go around them.

options.name: boss_randomization
options.description: Randomize Golden 4 bosses access doors using bidirectional access portals.

options.name: layout_patches
options.description: Include the anti-softlock layout patches. Disable at your own softlocking risk!

options.name: morph_placement
options.description: Influences where the Morphing Ball will be placed.

options.name: strict_minors
options.description:
Instead of using the Minors proportions as probabilities, enforce a strict distribution to match the proportions
as closely as possible.

options.name: missile_qty
options.description: The higher the number, the higher the probability of choosing Missiles when placing a minor.

options.name: super_qty
options.description: The higher the number, the higher the probability of choosing Super Missiles when placing a minor.

options.name: power_bomb_qty
options.description: The higher the number, the higher the probability of choosing Power Bombs when placing a minor.

options.name: minor_qty
options.description: From 7%, minimum number of minors required to finish the game, to 100%.

options.name: energy_qty
options.description:
Choose how many Energy/Reserve Tanks will be available, from 0-1 in ultra sparse, 4-6 in sparse, 8-12 in medium
and 18 in vanilla.

options.name: fun_combat
options.description:
Forces removal of Plasma Beam and Screw Attack if the preset and settings allow it. In addition, can randomly
remove Spazer and Wave Beam from the Combat set. If used, might force 'minimal' accessibility.

options.name: fun_movement
options.description:
Forces removal of Space Jump if the preset allows it. In addition, can randomly remove High Jump, Grappling Beam,
Spring Ball, Speed Booster, and Bombs from the Movement set. If used, might force 'minimal' accessibility.

options.name: fun_suits
options.description:
If the preset and seed layout allow it, will force removal of at least one of Varia Suit and/or Gravity Suit. If
used, might force 'minimal' accessibility.

options.name: varia_tweaks
options.description:
Include minor tweaks for the game to behave 'as it should' in a randomizer context:
- Bomb Torizo always activates after picking up its item and does not require Bomb to activate
- Wrecked Ship item on the Energy Tank Chozo statue is present before defeating Phantoon
- Lower Norfair Chozo statue that lowers the acid toward Gold Torizo does not require Space Jump to activate

options.name: gravity_behaviour
options.description:
Modify the heat damage and enemy damage reduction qualities of the Gravity and Varia Suits.
- Vanilla: Gravity provides full protection against all environmental damage (heat, spikes, etc.)
- Balanced: Removes Gravity environmental protection. Doubles Varia environmental protection. Enemy damage protection
is vanilla (50% Varia, 75% Gravity).
- Progressive: Gravity provides 50% heat reduction, Varia provides full heat reduction. Each suit adds 50% enemy
and environmental reduction, stacking to 75% reduction if you have both.

options.name: nerfed_charge
options.description:
Samus begins with a starter Charge Beam that does one third of charged shot damage that can damage bosses. Pseudo
Screws also do one third damage. Special Beam Attacks do normal damage but cost 3 Power Bombs instead of 1. Once the
Charge Beam item has been collected, it does full damage and special attacks are back to normal.

options.name: spin_jump_restart
options.description: Allows Samus to start spinning in mid air after jumping or falling.

options.name: rando_speed
options.description: Let Samus keeps her momentum when landing from a fall or from jumping.

options.name: infinite_space_jump
options.description: Space jumps can be done quicker and at any time in air, water or lava, even after falling long distances.

options.name: relaxed_round_robin_cf
options.description:
Changes Crystal Flashes behavior and requirements as follows:

You can perform a Crystal Flash with any amount of ammo, but you need at least one Power Bomb to begin the process.
After consuming 1 ammo, Samus gains 50 energy, and it will try a different ammo type next,  
cycling through Missiles, Supers, and Power Bombs as available. The cycling is to keep the consumption even between ammo types.
If one of your ammo types is at 0, it will be skipped.
The Crystal Flash ends when Samus is out of ammo or a total of 30 ammo has been consumed.

options.name: elevators_speed
options.description: Accelerate elevators transitions.

options.name: fast_doors
options.description: Accelerate doors transitions.

options.name: refill_before_save
options.description: Refill energy and ammo when saving.

options.name: hud
options.description:
Displays the current area name and the number of remaining items of selected item split in the HUD for the
current area.

options.name: hide_items
options.description:
Hides half of the visible items.
Items always visible:
- Energy Tank, Gauntlet
- Energy Tank, Terminator
- Morphing Ball
- Missile (Crateria moat)
- Missile (green Brinstar below super missile)
- Missile (above Crocomire)
- Power Bomb (lower Norfair above fire flea room)
- Missile (Gravity Suit)
- Missile (green Maridia shinespark)

options.name: no_music
options.description: Disable the background music.

options.name: random_music
options.description: Randomize the background music.

options.name: custom_preset
options.description:
see https://varia.run/presets for detailed info on each preset settings
knows: each skill (know) has a pair [can use, perceived difficulty using one of 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 each one
matching a max_difficulty]
settings: hard rooms, hellruns and bosses settings
controller: predefined controller mapping and moon walk setting

Share part of your item pool with other players.
Generic items plando.

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: completion_type
options.description: Set goal for game completion

options.name: area_rando
options.description: Randomize Entrances

options.name: buddy_checks
options.description: Bob-omb Buddies are checks, Cannon Unlocks are items

options.name: exclamation_boxes
options.description:
Include 1Up Exclamation Boxes during randomization.
Adds 29 locations to the pool.

options.name: progressive_keys
options.description: Keys will first grant you access to the Basement, then to the Second Floor

options.name: enable_coin_stars
options.description:
Determine logic for 100 Coin Stars.

Off - Removed from pool. You can still collect them, but they don't do anything.
Optimal for ignoring 100 Coin Stars entirely. Removes 15 locations from the pool.

On - Kept in pool, potentially randomized.

Vanilla - Kept in pool, but NOT randomized.

options.name: enable_locked_paintings
options.description:
Determine how paintings are treated.

Off - Paintings are not locked, as long as you can access them you can enter them (Vanilla behavior).

On - Paintings (other than BoB) start off locked and 11 stars are replaced in the pool with items to allow access to them.
Attempting to enter a locked painting will simply kick Mario out.
Does not affect secrets and levels that don't have a painting (BBH, HMC, RR).
This only affects the ability for Mario to enter a painting, the destination of the painting may change due to Entrance Randomization, if it is enabled.

options.name: strict_cap_requirements
options.description: If disabled, Stars that expect special caps may have to be acquired without the caps

options.name: strict_cannon_requirements
options.description:
If disabled, Stars that expect cannons may have to be acquired without them.
Has no effect if Buddy Checks and Move Randomizer are disabled

options.name: enable_move_rando
options.description:
Mario is unable to perform some actions until a corresponding item is picked up.
This option is incompatible with builds using a 'nomoverando' branch.
Specific actions to randomize can be specified in the YAML.

options.name: move_rando_actions
options.description: Which actions to randomize when Move Randomizer is enabled

options.name: strict_move_requirements
options.description:
If disabled, Stars that expect certain moves may have to be acquired without them. Only makes a difference
if Move Randomization is enabled

options.name: amount_of_stars
options.description:
How many stars exist.
If there aren't enough locations to hold the given total, the total will be reduced.

options.name: first_bowser_star_door_cost
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required at the Star Door to Bowser in the Dark World

options.name: basement_star_door_cost
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required at the Star Door in the Basement

options.name: second_floor_star_door_cost
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required to access the third floor

options.name: mips1_cost
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required to spawn MIPS the first time

options.name: mips2_cost
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required to spawn MIPS the second time.

options.name: stars_to_finish
options.description: What percent of the total stars are required at the infinite stairs

options.name: death_link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: ring_link
options.description: Whether your in-level coin gain/loss is linked to other players

options.name: trap_link
options.description: Whether your received traps are linked to other players

options.name: early_climb
options.description:
Force Climb to appear early in the seed as a local item.

This is particularly useful to prevent BK when Level Shuffle is disabled

options.name: goal
options.description:
Determines the goal of the seed

Bowser: Defeat Koopalings, reach Bowser's Castle and defeat Bowser

Yoshi Egg Hunt: Find a certain number of Yoshi Eggs

options.name: bosses_required
options.description: How many Bosses (Koopalings or Reznor) must be defeated in order to defeat Bowser

options.name: max_yoshi_egg_cap
options.description:
Maximum possible number of Yoshi Eggs that will be in the item pool

If fewer available locations exist in the pool than this number, the number of available locations will be used instead.

Required Percentage of Yoshi Eggs will be calculated based off of that number.

options.name: percentage_of_yoshi_eggs
options.description: What Percentage of Yoshi Eggs are required to finish Yoshi Egg Hunt

options.name: dragon_coin_checks
options.description: Whether collecting 5 Dragon Coins in each level will grant a check

options.name: moon_checks
options.description: Whether collecting a 3-Up Moon in a level will grant a check

options.name: hidden_1up_checks
options.description:
Whether collecting a hidden 1-Up mushroom in a level will grant a check

These checks are considered cryptic as there's no actual indicator that they're in their respective places

Enable this option at your own risk

options.name: bonus_block_checks
options.description: Whether collecting a 1-Up mushroom from a Bonus Block in a level will grant a check

options.name: blocksanity
options.description:
Whether hitting a block with an item or coin inside will grant a check

Note that some blocks are excluded due to how the option and the game works!

Exclusion list:
  * Blocks in Top Secret Area & Front Door/Bowser Castle
  * Blocks that are unreachable unless you glitch your way in

options.name: level_shuffle
options.description: Whether levels are shuffled

options.name: exclude_special_zone
options.description:
If active, this option will prevent any progression items from being placed in Special Zone levels.

Additionally, if Level Shuffle is active, Special Zone levels will not be shuffled away from their vanilla tiles.

options.name: bowser_castle_doors
options.description:
How the doors of Bowser's Castle behave

Vanilla: Front and Back Doors behave as vanilla

Fast: Both doors behave as the Back Door

Slow: Both doors behave as the Front Door

"Front Door" rooms depend on the `bowser_castle_rooms` option

"Back Door" only requires going through the dark hallway to Bowser

options.name: bowser_castle_rooms
options.description:
How the rooms of Bowser's Castle Front Door behave

Vanilla: You can choose which rooms to enter, as in vanilla

Random Two Room: Two random rooms are chosen

Random Five Room: Five random rooms are chosen

Gauntlet: All eight rooms must be cleared

Labyrinth: Which room leads to Bowser?

options.name: boss_shuffle
options.description:
How bosses are shuffled

None: Bosses are not shuffled

Simple: Four Reznors and the seven Koopalings are shuffled around

Full: Each boss location gets a fully random boss

Singularity: One or two bosses are chosen and placed at every boss location

options.name: swap_donut_gh_exits
options.description:
If enabled, this option will swap which overworld direction the two exits of the level at the Donut Ghost House overworld tile go:

False: Normal Exit goes up, Secret Exit goes right.

True: Normal Exit goes right, Secret Exit goes up.

options.name: junk_fill_percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of non-required Yoshi Eggs in the item pool with random junk items (only applicable on Yoshi Egg Hunt goal)

options.name: trap_fill_percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of junk items in the item pool with random traps

options.name: ice_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes the level to become slippery

options.name: stun_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which briefly stuns Mario

options.name: literature_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes the player to read literature

options.name: timer_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes the timer to run low

options.name: reverse_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes the controls to be reversed in the current level

options.name: thwimp_trap_weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes a Thwimp to spawn above the player

options.name: display_received_item_popups
options.description: What messages to display in-game for items received

options.name: autosave
options.description: Whether a save prompt will appear after every level

options.name: overworld_speed
options.description: How fast Mario moves on the overworld

options.name: music_shuffle
options.description:
Music shuffle type

None: No Music is shuffled

Consistent: Each music track is consistently shuffled throughout the game

Full: Each individual level has a random music track

Singularity: The entire game uses one song for overworld and one song for levels

options.name: sfx_shuffle
options.description:
Shuffles almost every instance of sound effect playback

Archipelago elements that play sound effects aren't randomized

None: No SFX are shuffled

Full: Each individual SFX call has a random SFX

Singularity: The entire game uses one SFX for every SFX call

options.name: mario_palette
options.description: Mario palette color

options.name: level_palette_shuffle
options.description:
Whether to shuffle level palettes

Off: Do not shuffle palettes

On Legacy: Uses only the palette sets from the original game

On Curated: Uses custom, hand-crafted palette sets

options.name: overworld_palette_shuffle
options.description:
Whether to shuffle overworld palettes

Off: Do not shuffle palettes

On Legacy: Uses only the palette sets from the original game

On Curated: Uses custom, hand-crafted palette sets

options.name: starting_life_count
options.description: How many extra lives to start the game with

options.name: sm_logic
options.description:
This option selects what kind of logic to use for item placement inside
Super Metroid.

Normal - Normal logic includes only what Super Metroid teaches players
itself. Anything that's not demonstrated in-game or by the intro cutscenes
will not be required here.

Hard - Hard logic is based upon the "no major glitches" ruleset and
includes most tricks that are considered minor glitches, with some 
restrictions. You'll want to be somewhat of a Super Metroid veteran for
this logic.

See https://samus.link/information for required moves.

options.name: sword_location
options.description:
This option decides where the first sword will be placed.
Randomized - The sword can be placed anywhere.
Early - The sword will be placed in a location accessible from the start of
the game.
Uncle - The sword will always be placed on Link's Uncle.

options.name: morph_location
options.description:
This option decides where the morph ball will be placed.
Randomized - The morph ball can be placed anywhere.
Early - The morph ball will be placed in a location accessible from the 
start of the game.
Original location - The morph ball will always be placed at its original 
location.

options.name: goal
options.description:
This option decides what goal is required to finish the randomizer.
Defeat Ganon and Mother Brain - Find the required crystals and boss tokens to kill both bosses.
Fast Ganon and Defeat Mother Brain - The hole to ganon is open without having to defeat Agahnim in 
                                     Ganon's Tower and Ganon can be defeat as soon you have the required 
                                     crystals to make Ganon vulnerable. For keysanity, this mode also removes 
                                     the Crateria Boss Key requirement from Tourian to allow faster access.
All Dungeons and Defeat Mother Brain -  Similar to "Defeat Ganon and Mother Brain", but also requires all dungeons 
                                        to be beaten including Castle Tower and Agahnim.

options.name: key_shuffle
options.description:
This option decides how dungeon items such as keys are shuffled.
None - A Link to the Past dungeon items can only be placed inside the 
dungeon they belong to, and there are no changes to Super Metroid.
Keysanity - See https://samus.link/information

options.name: open_tower
options.description:
The amount of crystals required to be able to enter Ganon's Tower. 
If this is set to Random, the amount can be found in-game on a sign next to Ganon's Tower.

options.name: ganon_vulnerable
options.description:
The amount of crystals required to be able to harm Ganon. The amount can be found 
in-game on a sign near the top of the Pyramid.

options.name: open_tourian
options.description:
The amount of boss tokens required to enter Tourian. The amount can be found in-game 
on a sign above the door leading to the Tourian entrance.

options.name: spin_jumps_animation
options.description: Enable separate space/screw jump animations

options.name: heart_beep_speed
options.description: Sets the speed of the heart beep sound in A Link to the Past.

options.name: heart_color
options.description: Changes the color of the hearts in the HUD for A Link to the Past.

options.name: quick_swap
options.description: When enabled, lets you switch items in ALTTP with L/R

options.name: energy_beep
options.description: Toggles the low health energy beep in Super Metroid.

options.name: difficulty
options.description: Changes relative spell cost and stuff

options.name: energy_core
options.description: How to obtain the Energy Core

options.name: required_fragments
options.description: Required fragment count for Energy Core = Fragments

options.name: available_fragments
options.description: Placed fragment count for Energy Core = Fragments

options.name: money_modifier
options.description: Money multiplier in %

options.name: exp_modifier
options.description: EXP multiplier for Weapons, Characters and Spells in %

options.name: sequence_breaks
options.description: Disable, enable some sequence breaks or put them in logic

options.name: out_of_bounds
options.description: Disable, enable the out-of-bounds glitch or put it in logic

options.name: fix_cheats
options.description: Fix cheats left in by the devs (not desert skip)

options.name: fix_infinite_ammo
options.description: Fix infinite ammo glitch

options.name: fix_atlas_glitch
options.description: Fix atlas underflowing stats

options.name: fix_wings_glitch
options.description: Fix wings making you invincible in some areas

options.name: shorter_dialogs
options.description: Cuts some dialogs

options.name: short_boss_rush
options.description: Start boss rush at Metal Magmar, cut enemy HP in half

options.name: ingredienizer
options.description: On Shuffles, Full randomizes spell ingredients

options.name: sniffamizer
options.description:
Off: all vanilla items in sniff spots
Shuffle: sniff items shuffled into random sniff spots
    Everywhere: add sniff spots to multiworld pool

options.name: sniff_ingredients
options.description: Select which items should be used as sniff items

options.name: callbeadamizer
options.description: On Shuffles call bead characters, Full shuffles individual spells

options.name: musicmizer
options.description: Randomize music for some rooms

options.name: doggomizer
options.description: On shuffles dog per act, Full randomizes dog per screen, Pupdunk gives you Everpupper everywhere

options.name: turdo_mode
options.description: Replace offensive spells by Turd Balls with varying strength and make weapons weak
